title: Cardiovascular Program Specialist - North Central (Future Opportunity)
description:
**CANDIATE MUST LIVE OR BE RELOCATABLE CLOSE TO A MAJOR AIRPORT IN THE NORTH CENTRAL SUCH AS NASHVILLE, INDIANAPOLIS, OR PITTSBURGH

Primary Function of Position
The Cardiovascular Program Specialist (CVPS) will provide expert clinical support, education, and training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci cardiac surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Cardiovascular Sales Manager (CVSM) to ensure safe and effective product adoption while driving positive patient outcomes. This role is part of a small team of strategic sales professionals across the country who are focused on developing cardiac surgeons, and all those associated with cardiac programs.

Clinical Support & Case Coverage

  • Provide on-site case support in the operating room or hybrid OR for procedures involving robotic cardiac procedures and surgery technologies.
  • Serve as a clinical expert for product setup, troubleshooting, and optimal use during live cases.
  • Ensure compliance with clinical and safety protocols.
  • Expand the user base collaborating with CVSM to cultivate a training pipeline of new surgeons.
  • Exhibit proficiency in multiple technology platforms to effectively support DaVinci adoption of Multiport Single Port, digital solutions, and customer needs.
  • Promote advanced instruments and accessories to enhance surgical performance and promote surgeon autonomy.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional internal teams to identify and capitalize on opportunities for expanding the use of the da Vinci® Surgical Systems and strengthening Intuitive's partnership with healthcare facilities.

Training & Education

  • Conduct training for physicians and care team members on indications and proper use of robotic platforms.
  • Administer individualized surgeon and care team training sessions onsite and assist with organizing appropriate mentoring programs.
  • Support new site start-ups by delivering onboarding programs and in-services.
  • Act as a resource for ongoing education and product updates.
  • Design and implement tailored da Vinci® pathways for surgeons and surgical teams to ensure proficient and autonomous system use, by providing recurring care team training as needed.
  • Maintain flexibility to support after-hours cases and provide weekend support as needed, dictated by the territory's adoption of robotic surgery.

Collaboration & Sales Partnership

  • Partner with local ISI sales team, leadership, customer training, and business partners to execute the appropriate clinical plan for surgeons and surgical teams to ensure system autonomy within a reasonable time frame
  • Provide clinical insights to the commercial team to shape strategy and drive business growth.
  • Participate in physician education programs, workshops, and regional/national conferences.
  • Facilitate the adoption of our digital solutions through enhancing our customer infrastructure and capabilities.
  • Communicate and collaborate with ancillary equipment manufacturers to develop strategies to ensure overall programmatic success

Market & Clinical Insights

  • Collect and communicate customer feedback to internal teams (sales, marketing, R&D).
  • Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
  • Assist in clinical trial support when required.

Required Education, Skills, Experience

Education: Bachelor’s degree in nursing, Life Sciences, or related field required.

Advanced degrees (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) preferred.

Preferred Skills and Experience

    • Deep understanding of cardiac anatomy, physiology, and interventional procedures.
    • Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
    • Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
    • Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
    • Ability to work in high-pressure environments (OR/Cath lab)
    • Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
    • Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
    • Willingness to travel up to 75% domestically.


We provide market-competitive compensation packages, inclusive of base pay, incentives, benefits, and equity.

On Target Earnings: $200K

title: Senior/ Lead Full-stack Developer
description:
Roles & Responsibilities

COMPANY: Spatial Intelligence for Design (DP Architects Pte Ltd)

THE FUTURE OF ARCHITECTURE Sid is a startup incubated within DP Architects that’s building tech at the forefront of architecture. We have already released Nimble Façade, the easiest way to automatically calculate the efficiency of building façades, but that’s just the start. We are developing proprietary AI-driven technology to process all kinds of construction data, which we are using to power many more products at various stages of development. This is not your average architectural practice playing lip service to digital transformation. We are a revenue-generating startup, backed by a global architecture firm, building technology for how architects and engineers will get their work done in the years to come.

OUR MISSION Sid exists to make supercharged technology accessible to architects, engineers, and built-environment professionals — empowering them todo their best work, transform their profession, and uplift the lives of everyone in the buildings they create.

JOB SUMMARY: You’d be working with users at DP Architects, partner organisations and Sid’s customers to build products on top of our underlying technology, as well as improving that technology where needed. We build and validate ideas quickly before deploying and scaling them as we roll out to more users. You’ll be helping us across the whole lifecycle so, while you will primarily be building web apps using TypeScript and Angular, you’ll also be involved in shaping the product itself. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Architect, design and build high-quality software at all parts of the lifecycle from prototypes, production through iteration Build both the Angular frontends and the RESTful APIs that power them Get involved in every aspect of the software development lifecycle, we’re a small team so you’ll need to manage your own time well Contribute to technical architecture and systems design, helping to set high standards for yourself and the team Collaborate with other engineers as well as product, design, architects and clients to scope the solution so that what you build solves real pain points We use LLMs to help us write code, but you should understand and approve every line of code that you push PREFERRED SKILLS: Strong understanding of TypeScript and a frontend framework (we use modern Angular but it’s easy to pick up if you know React) Good knowledge of databases (we primarily use Postgres, but an understanding of different databases is a plus!) Experience with CI/CD, Git, deploying to cloud environments and scaling production systems As a bonus, experience with Python (many of the behind-the-scenes processing is done via Python, though we can help you upskill if you don’t have a good grasp of Python!) As a bonus, any experience with construction engineering or 3D modelling software Communication is important within a small team and is a core skill for this role alongside technical knowledge Despite being incubated within DP Architects we are a startup, any experience with a fast-paced environment where priorities shift often is a plus We value people who are independent thinkers and problem solvers, so if you don’t see yourself exactly in the job spec above, you can show how you have learned and overcome problems in your career. We value diverse experiences and candidates who have the willingness to approach new challenges. Let’s chat about how you might fit into our team. WORK ENVIRONMENT: We work together in the office five days a week because collaboration is central to how we operate. At the same time, we are committed to work-life balance and respecting boundaries. We offer flexibility to work from home when needed. Tell employers what skills you have Collaborate With Engineers hands-on skills Software Build Architect Built Environment Job Descriptions Ideas Development Angular (Web Framework) Team Leadership Engineering Time Management Technical Architecture shaping Liaising With Architects Code Analysis React.js

title: Associate/Senior Editor, BMC Biomedical Engineering
description:
Role: Associate/Senior Editor, BMC Biomedical Engineering

Location: New York or Shanghai- Hybrid, Permanent

Closing date: September 14, 2026

About Springer Nature

Springer Nature is one of the leading publishers of research in the world. We publish the largest number of journals and books and are pioneers in open research. Through our leading brands, trusted for more than 180 years, we provide technology-enabled products, platforms and services that help researchers to uncover new ideas and share their discoveries, health professionals to stay at the forefront of medical science, and educators to advance learning. We are proud to be part of progress, working together with the communities we serve to share knowledge and bring greater understanding to the world.

For more information, For more information, please visit about.springernature.com and @SpringerNature.

At Springer Nature, we recognise that talent is developed through a range of career paths. We encourage applications from individuals with strong transferable skills, provided they are supported by relevant experience that shows how those skills have been successfully applied in practice. Our hiring approach balances skills, experience, and potential to ensure each role is fulfilled with both short term effectiveness and long-term growth in mind.

About the Brand

BMC has more than 25 years of experience in developing open access and provides high-quality, impactful research and a supportive publishing experience for authors. We are committed to publishing the best open access journals in our portfolio of over 250 titles and we strive to drive progress in biology, health sciences and medicine. Visit biomedcentral.com and follow @BioMedCentral

About the Role

As an Associate or Senior Editor you will contribute to the success of our journals by supporting editorial handling of content across a defined portfolio of journals and by driving the content development of these journals. This is a dynamic and varied role that will give you the opportunity to see content across a broad range of topics and contribute to the success of BMC as a whole.

Role Responsibilities

  • Handle original research manuscripts, applying critical scientific evaluation to assess quality, novelty, and suitability for publication while managing manuscript selection and peer review processes.

  • Drive editorial excellence by delivering high-quality editorial services in accordance with journal standards, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and adherence to publication timelines.

  • Manage and optimize publishing workflows and systems to support efficient manuscript processing, peer review, decision-making, and publication activities.

  • Collaborate closely with authors, reviewers, and editorial board members to ensure a rigorous and transparent review process while maintaining strong stakeholder relationships.

  • Serve as a key representative of the journal within the scientific community, engaging with researchers and industry experts to understand emerging trends, priorities, and publishing needs.

  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of editorial policies, peer review practices, and publishing processes to uphold scientific integrity and enhance the journal's impact and reputation.

  • Communicate clearly and effectively with authors, Editorial Board Members, and reviewers, guiding stakeholders through the peer review process, delivering decisions with clarity, and leveraging strong collaboration and interpersonal awareness to foster productive relationships.

  • Build trusted partnerships with internal and external stakeholders while managing competing priorities and expectations, applying conflict management and relationship-building skills to drive alignment, resolve challenges, and ensure smooth editorial operations

  • Partner with the Chief Editor to execute the journal’s development strategy, leveraging market intelligence and a strategic mindset to identify growth opportunities, strengthen journal positioning, and support long-term objectives.

  • Drive content development by proactively attracting high-quality submissions, commissioning reviews and special collections, and collaborating with the scientific community to advance impactful publishing initiatives and enhance journal influence.

  • Represent BMC and Springer Nature within the global research community by attending conferences, engaging with research institutions, and leveraging strong communication skills to promote journal visibility, foster relationships, and attract high-quality submissions.

  • Develop compelling scientific and academic content to showcase published research, while contributing to a collaborative editorial culture by sharing expertise, supporting colleagues, and driving knowledge exchange across the BMC editorial team.

To be considered we encourage applications from candidates who meet most, but not necessarily all, of the criteria.

Skills, Experience & Qualifications

Essential

  • Educated to PhD level (or equivalent), in a biomedical field
  • Effective time management and prioritization skills
  • Analytical/critical thinking skills
  • Excellent communication and influencing skills
  • Customer focused attitude
  • Willing to travel occasionally and represent BMC at external events
  • Flexible mindset
  • Ability to work cooperatively with colleagues at all levels and across Springer Nature

Desirable

  • A can-do approach to problem-solving
  • An interest in open access publishing
  • Knowledge of editorial processes

In return, we offer a competitive salary range and great employee benefits.

To Apply: Applicants should include the following:

  • an updated CV

  • a cover letter explaining their interest in the post

Springer Nature US provides a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes the benefit offerings listed below:

  • Medical, Dental and Vision

  • 401(k) with company match and contribution

  • Hybrid office working policy, Summer Hours, and paid time off

  • Flexible Spending and Commuter programs

  • Multiple Life insurance options

  • Disability coverage

  • Tuition Assistance

  • Voluntary benefits: Identity Theft Protection, Pet Insurance, and Legal Assistance Insurance

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Family friendly benefits and a variety of employee discounts

  • An array of Employee Social Networks

US Annualized Base Salary Range: Associate Editor: $80,000 / Senior Editor: $95,000.The salary offer may vary based on work experience, education, skill level and equity. The US salary range does not align with the salary ranges in other countries when converted to the currency of that country.

title: Clinical Trial Liaison, Director – West
location: Wilmington, Delaware, United States of America
description:
US Field Based

AstraZeneca is advancing the pace of Clinical Trial progress in the US as a critical enabler of Ambition 2030. The Regional Director, Clinical Trial Liaison Team will lead and manage a field-based Clinical Trial Liaison team responsible for strengthening scientific engagement with strategic clinical research sites, improving investigator understanding of AstraZeneca trials and pipeline, and helping reduce practical barriers to study start-up, screening, enrollment, referral, and retention.

This role blends Field Medical Affairs leadership with deep clinical trial partnership. The Regional Director will translate national Clinical Trial Liaison priorities into regional execution, aligning with BioPharmaceuticals Business Unit US Medical headquarters and field teams, Clinical Value and Outcomes, US Site Management and Monitoring, Clinical Operations, and other matrix partners to deliver coordinated site-facing engagement.

The Regional Director will coach and develop a regional Clinical Trial Liaison team that advances high-quality engagement across priority US research centers. The role is accountable for recommending priority site selection, and setting up a clear field plans consistent engagement expectations across US strategic research centers increasing the consistency, impact, and speed of site-facing medical support for new and ongoing clinical studies across AstraZeneca marketed products, new indications, and compounds in development, including priorities across Cardiovascular, Renal and Metabolic; Respiratory, Immunology; and Vaccines and Infectious Disease.

The Regional Director is accountable for field performance, team health, and executional excellence across the assigned region. The leader will set expectations, coach to quality, assess capability needs, and create a culture of accountability, collaboration, compliance, and urgency in support of US clinical trial acceleration.

The role will represent investigator, site, and referring-provider perspectives in Medical Affairs and clinical trial workstreams, ensuring that site-facing engagement remains aligned to trial priorities, regional realities, and the broader ambition to accelerate access to innovative medicines for patients.

Key Accountabilities

  • Team Leadership: Lead and coach a regional Clinical Trial Liaison team through clear goals, call plans, ride-alongs, timely feedback, onboarding, capability building, and talent development.

  • Drive Performance and Lead execution: Establish performance expectations, monitor execution against priorities, use metrics and field observations to identify gaps, and coach the team toward improved impact, engagement consistency, and accountability.

  • Manage Talent: Recruit, onboard, develop, and retain high-performing Clinical Trial Liaisons while fostering accountability, collaboration, and team health.

  • Strengthen CTL Site Engagement: Strengthen scientific engagement with clinical investigators, thought leaders, health care professionals, site staff, and referring physicians to improve understanding of trial protocols, study designs, pipeline assets, and study compounds.

  • Strong Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner with US Site Management and Monitoring, Clinical Operations, headquarter and global medical teams, MSLs and Clinical Account Directors, and Medical Affairs partners to deliver coordinated site-facing engagement

  • Accelerate Insights to Action: Ensure field insights from investigators and research sites are captured with quality, shared rapidly with the appropriate national and headquarters partners, and translated into practical field actions.

  • Lead Change Adoption and Execution: Implement R&D initiatives, remove execution barriers, and reinforce ways of working through training and consistent field follow-up.

  • Resource and Compliance Management: Manage regional resources, travel, congress activity, and spend while ensuring adherence to AstraZeneca policies, Medical Affairs standards, and FDA requirements.

Essential Requirements

  • Advanced degree in a scientific or clinical discipline, such as MD, DO, PharmD, PhD, NP, or PA-C, or equivalent advanced health practitioner experience.

  • 3+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry, Field Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, or clinical trial research, with a portion of that experience leading teams or demonstrating strong leadership capability.

  • Strong experience with clinical research, study site logistics, investigator and site engagement, and collaboration with clinical operations partners.

  • Working knowledge of FDA compliance, regulatory requirements, Medical Affairs policies, and appropriate scientific exchange standards.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate national strategy into regional account coverage, field plans, and measurable execution priorities.

  • Established track record of effective and influential scientific communication, including oral presentations to health care professionals and internal stakeholders.

  • Excellent interpersonal, oral, written, project management, and change leadership skills.

  • Ability to synthesize field insights, identify execution barriers, and communicate recommended actions clearly across a matrix organization.

  • Ability to travel 30-40% of the time, with travel requirements varying by geography and business need.

Desirable Requirements

  • Doctorate in bio-sciences, pharmacology, pharmacy, nursing, medicine, or a related clinical or scientific field.

  • Previous line management experience in Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, or Field Medical Affairs.

  • Three or more years of Medical Science Liaison experience.

  • Experience in pharmaceutical industry clinical or preclinical research, drug discovery, drug development, pipeline engagement, or key external expert interactions.

  • Experience working in an account-based setting with Commercial Account Directors and other internal matrix partners.

  • Experience with clinical trial site education, investigator engagement, feasibility input, patient recruitment initiatives, or trial-enrollment support.

  • Entrepreneurial, future-forward attitude with enthusiasm for coaching, change adoption, and advancing patient care.

Why AstraZeneca?

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That's why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility.

In addition, our positions offer a short-term incentive bonus opportunity; eligibility to participate in our equity-based long-term incentive program. The year 1954 marked a significant milestone in thermal insulation history. Armstrong’s R&D Project Number 54013, developed by three innovators, evolved into ArmaFlex, the world's first flexible, closed-cell elastomeric foam for equipment insulation. This product revolutionized the insulation industry. Today, more than 70 years later, ArmaFlex continues to be a pillar of Armacell's success.

The Production Planner is a key member of the Mebane team reporting to the Plant Supply Chain Manager. The Production Planner role is responsible for all aspects of planning, scheduling, managing the service level, costs and inventories for products that run on production lines. The planner works closely with the other production planners, the raw materials manager, suppliers, manufacturing, the distribution center, and customer service personnel as necessary. This position is responsible for balancing customer service, inventory levels within inventory turn targets, and the efficient utilization of production/distribution facilities, manpower and working capital in assigned areas.

  • Healthcare benefits including medical & prescription drug coverage, dental, vision, and mental health & wellbeing.

  • Financial programs such as 401(k), life insurance, short & long- term disability coverage, and opportunities for performance-based salary incentive programs.

  • Paid time off including 12 holidays and generous PTO.

  • Training and educational resources on our personalized learning management system.

  • Giving & volunteer opportunities, and discounts on retail products, services & experiences.

Job Responsibilities

  • Create and publish weekly production plans for manufacturing lines

  • Provide 6-8 week planning horizons to support production line plans and raw material requirements

  • Maintain planning and inventory parameters that optimize SAP to provide best in class results

  • Collaborate with Customer Service, Planning, Procurement and inventory control to service the customers with the best availability dates possible

  • Periodically review and update SAP master data tables, particularly ABC class and safety stock settings and throughput rates for capacity planning

  • Communicate with Customer Service when orders will not be delivered as expected

  • Knowledgeable with SAP / AIMS / Advise software and creation of Process Orders

  • Work with the Sales Team and Production to create new production items and set them up in SAP

  • Actively pursue continuous improvement and support company initiatives, such as World Class Armacell Mindset (WAM)

  • Provide reports that gauge the overall health of these business segments

  • Manage inventory levels to meet targets, including participation in and management of cycle count activities

  • Bachelor's Degree in Industrial Engineering, Logistics, Accounting or related field or equivalent level of knowledge typically gained by 5+ years’ practical job experience in a similar role

  • 2-5 years of production planning experience in a manufacturing environment required

  • Ability to excel in a cross-cultural, global team environment

  • Possesses professional written and verbal communication skills

  • Possesses strong analytical and problem-solving skills

  • Knowledge of SAP and Advise/Mesabi is preferred

  • Ability to work independently and multi-task in a fast-paced environment

  • Knowledge of Microsoft Office applications

  • Solid understanding of statistical process control and world class manufacturing techniques

  • Knowledge of rubber processing: mixing, curing, extrusion, and foaming

  • Proven experience in creating effective technical solutions

This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Cardiovascular Sales Manager (CVSM) to ensure safe and effective product adoption while driving positive patient outcomes. Clinical Support & Case Coverage

  • Serve as a clinical expert for product setup, troubleshooting, and optimal use during live cases.
  • Ensure compliance with clinical and safety protocols.
  • Expand the user base collaborating with CVSM to cultivate a training pipeline of new surgeons.
  • Exhibit proficiency in multiple technology platforms to effectively support DaVinci adoption of Multiport Single Port, digital solutions, and customer needs.

Training & Education

  • Administer individualized surgeon and care team training sessions onsite and assist with organizing appropriate mentoring programs.

  • Act as a resource for ongoing education and product updates.
  • Design and implement tailored da Vinci® pathways for surgeons and surgical teams to ensure proficient and autonomous system use, by providing recurring care team training as needed.
  • Maintain flexibility to support after-hours cases and provide weekend support as needed, dictated by the territory's adoption of robotic surgery.

Waipapa Taumata Rau | The University of Auckland

The University of Auckland creates globally transformative impacts through its distinctive strengths in world-leading research, scholarship, teaching and collaborative partnerships, inspired by its unique position in Aotearoa New Zealand and the Asia-Pacific.

Join New Zealand’s top-ranked and triple-crown accredited Auckland Business and Economics School, with an international reputation for shaping the future of research and teaching excellence, and be part of its continued growth as you embark on the next phase of your academic career. With strong growth in student numbers and sustained investment across the Faculty of Business and Economics, this is an exciting time to join as it continues to strengthen and expand its academic community.

Te Whiwhinga mahi | The opportunity

As the Faculty continues to grow, the Department of Economics is seeking an ambitious, collegial, and research-active Lecturer, (i.e. tenure-track Assistant Professor), Senior Lecturer or Associate Professor specialising in applied econometrics, microeconometrics and/or macroeconometrics.

The successful candidate will demonstrate strong research potential and a commitment to excellent, research-informed teaching, enhanced by appropriate learning technologies. You will contribute to an exceptional learning experience for undergraduate and postgraduate students, teaching in your specialist area and more widely at introductory levels, while developing your academic profile through research, publication and supervision of research students.

You will be encouraged to build research partnerships, seek external funding and engage with professional, academic and non-academic communities. You will contribute to an intellectually vibrant academic environment through interdisciplinary collaboration, knowledge exchange and departmental service, with opportunities to work across and beyond the Department.

All candidates will bring the potential to contribute service and citizenship within and beyond the University, as well as to actively participate in Department, Faculty and University committees and activities.

The faculty attracts high-calibre students to our world-class undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. We take pride in the excellence demonstrated by our internationally recognised scholars, who lead a vibrant research ecosystem supported by interdisciplinary research centres and a global network of visiting experts who contribute to both teaching and research.

This is a full-time (40 hours per week) permanent position (subject to continuation).

Remuneration depends on experience and achievements, and will be aligned with our Academic Standards policy. It will be within the following ranges:

Lecturer (L): NZ$99,788 - NZ$119,204
Senior Lecturer (SL): NZ$126,863 - NZ$158,904
Associate Professor (AP): From NZ$165,808

For more detailed information on the role accountabilities and requirements, please review the Position Description.

He kōrero mōu | About you

You will be a collegial academic with excellent communication skills and the ability to clearly articulate your ideas, research, and future plans. The successful appointee will have a PhD in Economics (or be near completion), with demonstrated excellence in research and a commitment to high quality research-informed teaching. title: Research Scientist II
description:

Department

(OPQS) - Health Data Innovation

Job Description:

Responsibilities

The Research Scientist II (Health Informatics) will work within the Office of Science, Center for Health Informatics to conduct research and coordinate the NICS surveillance efforts using NICS data and other data sources for mental health conditions that that may disqualify an individual from possessing or receiving a firearm under federal law. The Research Scientist II will coordinate with the New York State Office of Mental Health and will work closely with facilities that are under authority of Public Health Law Article 28 and Mental Hygiene Law (MHL) Article 31 on involuntary hospitalizations reporting to NICS, and will be responsible for NICS grant deliverables. The Research Scientist II will conduct research to validate and refine NICS monitoring, create and modify SAS or Python programs, generate surveillance reports, and monitor alerts to detect reporting errors that could result in preventable gun violence. The Research Scientist II will help maintain the NICS report module, NICSMAN, research and enhance data quality detection methods, create NICS surveillance reports, update user guides and documents, and train facility staff. The Research Scientist II will prepare peer-reviewed presentations, abstracts, and publications for best practices of public health surveillance using involuntary mental health admission data. Other appropriate related duties.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Computer Science, Public Health, or a related field and three years of research experience; OR a Master’s degree in a related field and two years of research experience; OR a Doctorate in a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

At least three years of experience in the areas of public health, medical or healthcare informatics, including clinical or public health data quality assessment, control, management and analysis, and health information technology. At least two years use of clinical data, including coding systems (e.g., ICD-9), data analytic, and HL7 data-interchange standard. At least two years of experience examining and cleansing data for completeness and accuracy, extracting pertinent data from existing systems, and preparing tables and clear narrative descriptions of the data and the analysis using SAS software, R, or Python. Excellent verbal and written communication skills demonstrated by at least two years of experience preparing reports, delivering presentations, and communicating and working with internal and external stakeholders.

Conditions of Employment

Grant funded position. Compliance with funding requirements such as time and effort reporting, grant deliverables, and contract deliverables, is required.


Visa sponsorship may be available for this position, in accordance with applicable federal requirements.

Travel up to 10% of the time will be required.


The selected candidate must reside within a reasonable commuting distance of the official work location specified in the job posting and must also be located in or willing to relocate to one of the following states: New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Vermont, or Massachusetts, prior to hire.

This position is eligible for a hybrid work schedule, with a combination of onsite and remote work.


HRI participates in the E-Verify Program


Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer/Qualified Individuals with Disabilities/Qualified Protected Veterans


www.healthresearch.org

Join us in our mission to make a difference in public health and advance scientific research! At Health Research, Inc. Depending on the regional scope of the role and exact function specifications, Analysts will work within international team settings with team members located across offices in various geographies.

  • Maintain accurate records and protect the confidentiality of all guest information.
  • Support Front Desk, Concierge, Guest Services, and In-Room Dining operations as needed.

title: BCLS Associate
description:
FULL TIME POSITION: Associate (Investment Team)

LOCATION: Boston, MA

BAIN CAPITAL OVERVIEW

With approximately $225 billion of assets under management, Bain Capital is one of the world’s leading private investment firms. We create lasting impact for our investors, teams, businesses, and the communities in which we live. Over four decades we have strategically grown our platform to focus on Private Equity, Growth & Venture, Capital Solutions, Credit, and Real Assets. Today, our team includes 1,980+ employees in 24 offices on four continents.

We partner differently to help people and companies embrace possibility and realize potential. Founded as a private partnership in 1984, we have fostered a culture of innovation, entrepreneurialism, and agility, empowering our people to define and own their career trajectories. Today, our partnership approach enables us to pursue strategic growth, build enduring relationships with a robust external network, and collaborate across our integrated platform to connect the deep and diverse expertise that unlocks breakthrough insights.

Our people are the heart of our advantage. Colleagues at all levels have a seat at the table as they tackle business challenges with a principal investor mindset. By asking incisive questions, respectfully challenging one another, and remaining intellectually agile, we work together to achieve exceptional outcomes.

LIFE SCIENCES OVERVIEW & POSITION OVERVIEW

Bain Capital Life Sciences (“BCLS”) focuses on making outstanding long-term investments in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, medical device, diagnostics, and life science technology companies globally. Our guiding principles are to invest in companies focused on helping patients with significant unmet medical needs, driving distinctive innovation, and creating exceptional investor returns. Our team differentiates itself through the depth and breadth of its experience in both private and public equity investing, as well as industry.

Our investment process places particular emphasis on rigorous analysis of pre-clinical and clinical research, strategic positioning, competitive dynamics, business model sustainability, and management team alignment and capability. Beyond the initial investment, our team stays closely involved with portfolio companies, providing ongoing strategic and operational support aimed at driving durable growth and value creation.

Associates on our Boston-based team work at the intersection of scientific diligence and investment decision-making, evaluating opportunities and contributing meaningfully to how we invest. Associates engage in the full investment process: building relationships of impact in the biomedical ecosystem, identifying distinctive investment ideas, leading diligence calls with KOLs and management teams, evaluating the underlying science, building the financial and strategic analysis that informs the deal potential and structure, facilitating Investment Committee discussions, and moving deals toward a decision. Our deal flow spans early-stage venture investments through complex public and private equity transactions, giving Associates broad exposure across investment types. Associates work across therapeutic areas and play critical roles on multiple deal teams simultaneously, learning from and working alongside our experienced team of senior investment professionals.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Evaluate investment opportunities end-to-end, exercising judgment on where the data supports conviction
  • Assess pre-clinical and clinical data, competitive dynamics, and scientific risk to form an investment view
  • Build and maintain financial models that inform how deals are priced, structured, and sized
  • Lead diligence calls with KOLs, management teams, and outside experts, focusing on the issues most critical to the investment thesis
  • Design and field industry surveys and other primary research to answer open questions in diligence
  • Prepare memos and materials to facilitate internal Investment Committee decision-making
  • Partner with portfolio company management teams on value creation initiatives
  • Attend investor conferences and medical meetings, engaging with physicians and peer investors to build industry insights and source compelling investment opportunities

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Strong academic credentials (BS/BA/MS/PhD and/or MD from a highly regarded institution) and demonstrated passion for and depth in biomedical or chemical sciences
  • 3+ years of professional experience in a scientific/medical field (academia or industry), consulting, and/or investing/investment banking/equity research
  • Strong analytical and quantitative skills
  • Creative approach to problem solving and demonstrated strategic thinking
  • Exceptionally strong written and verbal communication
  • High integrity, commitment, and work ethic
  • Self-motivated, collaborative, entrepreneurial, and comfortable taking ownership

COMPENSATION:

Expected Annual Base Salary: $150,000

Actual base salary will be determined by a wide range of factors including but not limited to role, function, level, experience, qualifications, and geographic location. In addition to a competitive base salary, this position may be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus based upon factors such as individual impact, team and firm performance. Bain Capital offers a competitive benefits package designed to support employees’ health, financial security, family needs, and overall well-being.

Bain Capital is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

title: Serviceinriktad leveransmedarbetare - Newport Premium Delivery
description:
Har du en naturlig känsla för service och trivs med en roll som kombinerar praktiskt arbete, kundkontakt och stort eget ansvar? Vill du arbeta med Newport Premium Delivery – vår premiumtjänst för möbelleveranser med personlig service hela vägen in i kundens hem? Då kan du vara den vi söker.

För att trivas i rollen är du driven, flexibel och strukturerad. Du har ett öga för detaljer och känner stolthet i att varje leverans genomförs med högsta kvalitet och service.

Newport är ett svenskägt företag som äger och utvecklar livsstilsvarumärket Newport. Företaget designar och säljer hemtextilier, inredningsdetaljer och möbler i det övre kvalitetssegmentet, både i Sverige och på internationella marknader. Med en etablerad global e-handel erbjuder Newport kunder över hela världen ett exklusivt och handplockat sortiment.

I koncernen ingår en butikskedja med åtta fysiska butiker. Newports flagshipbutik finns på Nordiska Kompaniet i Stockholm och övriga butiker finns i Göteborg, Västerås, Linköping, Norrköping, Steninge och Åre. Koncernen omsätter cirka 450 miljoner kronor.

Om tjänsten:

Som leveransmedarbetare för Newport Premium Delivery ser du till att våra möbler levereras och installeras hos kunden på ett tryggt, professionellt och förstklassigt sätt.

Du ansvarar för att möblerna hanteras varsamt, kommer fram i perfekt skick samt monteras och placeras korrekt i kundens hem. Rollen innebär både körning, praktiskt arbete och nära kundkontakt. Du behöver därför vara lika trygg bakom ratten som i mötet med människor.

Du blir en viktig representant för Newport och ser till att kundens upplevelse håller högsta nivå – från leverans till färdig möblering.


Arbetsuppgifter:

  • Leverera möbler till kunder på ett säkert och effektivt sätt.
  • Hantera och transportera möbler med stor omsorg.
  • Montera och placera möbler i kundens hem.
  • Forsla bort transportemballage och vid behov hantera utbyten av möbler.
  • Ge kunden ett professionellt, personligt och serviceinriktat bemötande.
  • Koordinera leveranser tillsammans med lager, kundtjänst och övriga berörda funktioner.
  • Bidra till att utveckla och förbättra Newport Premium Delivery.


Kvalifikationer:

  • B-körkort. C-körkort är meriterande.
  • God fysik och förmåga att hantera tunga lyft.
  • Ett ansvarstagande och lösningsorienterat arbetssätt med stort fokus på service.
  • Goda kunskaper i svenska och engelska.

Erfarenhet av möbelleveranser, transport, montering eller liknande arbete är meriterande, men inget krav. För oss är din inställning, ansvarskänsla och vilja att ge kunden en förstklassig upplevelse minst lika viktiga.


Vi erbjuder:

  • En ansvarsfull och varierad roll där ingen dag är den andra lik.
  • Ett praktiskt arbete med stort eget ansvar och många kundmöten.
  • En arbetsplats där kvalitet, service och engagemang står i centrum.
  • Vid behov hjälpa till med andra vanligt förekommande arbetsuppgifter på lagret.
  • Möjlighet att vara med och utveckla Newports premiumtjänst för möbelleveranser.


Placering och arbetstider

Tjänsten utgår från Newports centrallager i Norrköping och innebär resor till kunder, främst i mellersta Sverige. Arbetstiderna varierar och planeras utifrån bokade leveranser. Rollen kräver därför flexibilitet när det gäller både arbetstider och resor.

Tillträde sker omgående. Skicka din ansökan och ditt CV till work@newport.se

Urval och intervjuer sker löpande. Välkommen med din ansökan!


Om Newport

Newport grundades 1995 och är idag ett av Sveriges 100 största e-handelsbolag, med åtta fysiska butiker och en starkt växande global e-handel. Företaget designar och säljer möbler, hemtextilier och inredningsdetaljer i det övre kvalitetssegmentet, med en klassisk och tidlös stil präglad av internationell känsla.

Verksamheten bedrivs i egen regi och omfattar allt från varumärkes- och produktutveckling till marknadsföring, försäljning och distribution. Huvudkontoret och centrallagret finns i Norrköping.

title: Key Carrier Coordinator
description:
HomeGoods

At TJX Companies, every day brings new opportunities for growth, exploration, and achievement. You’ll be part of our vibrant team that embraces diversity, fosters collaboration, and prioritizes your development. Whether you’re working in our four global Home Offices, Distribution Centers or Retail Stores—TJ Maxx, Marshalls, Homegoods, Homesense, Sierra, Winners, and TK Maxx, you’ll find abundant opportunities to learn, thrive, and make an impact. Come join our TJX family—a Fortune 100 company and the world’s leading off-price retailer.

Job Description:

Opportunity: Grow Your Career

The Key Carrier role is an elevated extension of the Coordinator role. Key Carriers alternate their role based on store needs, predominantly performing the role of Coordinator and occasionally acting as Key Carrier, taking on a leadership role in maintaining all aspects of the store. Key Carriers must have open availability, including nights and weekends. Role models exceptional customer service.

  • Creates a positive internal and external customer experience
  • Promotes a culture of honesty and integrity; maintains confidentiality
  • Acts as Manager on Duty adhering to company policy and procedure
  • Ensures store team performs tasks and activities in accordance with store plan; prioritizes as needed
  • Addresses immediate customer service issues and provides appropriate coaching to Associates
  • Exercises discretion regarding customer service policies to satisfy customers
  • Maintains accurate Associate coverage in service areas for a positive customer experience
  • Ensures Associates adhere to all operational procedures
  • Ensures opening/closing procedures are executed according to company guidelines
  • Communicates accurately and effectively with management and Associates when setting and addressing priorities; provides progress updates
  • Provides and accepts recognition and constructive feedback
  • Provides feedback, recognition and coaching to Associates
  • Partners with Management on Associate training needs to increase effectiveness
  • Ensures adherence to all labor laws, policies, and procedures
  • Promotes credit and loyalty programs
  • Supports and participates in shrink reduction goals and programs
  • Promotes safety awareness and maintains a safe environment
  • Other duties as assigned

Who We’re Looking For: You.

  • Able to work a flexible schedule, including nights and weekends
  • Team player, working effectively with peers and supervisors
  • Able to respond appropriately to changes in direction or unexpected situations
  • Knowledge of company standard software, systems, and procedures
  • Knowledge of merchandise flow in stores
  • Proven problem solving skills
  • Able to effectively coach, delegate, and follow-up on multiple people/tasks
  • Able to act quickly under challenging circumstances
  • Capable of multi-tasking
  • Superior communication and organizational skills with attention to detail
  • 1 year retail, 6 months leadership experience

Benefits include: Associate discount; EAP; smoking cessation; bereavement; 401(k) Associate contributions; child care & cell phone discounts; pet & legal insurance; credit union; referral bonuses. Those who meet service or hours requirements are also eligible for: 401(k) match; medical/dental/vision; HSA; health care FSA; life insurance; short/long term disability; paid parental leave; paid holidays/vacation/sick; auto/home insurance discounts; scholarship program; adoption assistance. All benefits are provided in accordance with and subject to the terms of the applicable plan or program and may change from time to time. Contact your TJX representative for more information.

In addition to our open door policy and supportive work environment, we also strive to provide a competitive salary and benefits package. TJX considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, gender identity and expression, marital or military status, or based on any individual's status in any group or class protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. TJX also provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and applicable state and local law.

Applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment.

Address:

320 South Jordan Creek Pkwy Ste 300

Location:

USA HomeGoods Store 0662 West Des Moines IA

This position has a starting pay range of $15.25 to $15.75 per hour. Actual starting pay is determined by a number of factors, including relevant skills, qualifications, and experience.

title: Senior Workplace Engineer – Microsoft 365
description:
Senior Workplace Engineer – Microsoft 365

Are you an experienced workplace engineer with deep expertise in Microsoft 365, enterprise AI productivity tools, and automation? Do you enjoy resolving complex technical challenges while designing scalable solutions that improve the employee experience? If you thrive in a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of M365, Copilot, identity, endpoint management, and AI-enabled support, we want you on our team.

At Thomson Reuters, the Senior Workplace Engineer will provide third-line support and hands-on engineering for the internal Microsoft 365 and AI productivity stack. This role will resolve complex M365 and Copilot issues at the source while building the automation, integrations, and AI capabilities that improve service reliability and enhance the internal employee experience at scale.

You will serve as the senior escalation point for Microsoft 365 and AI-related issues, owning incidents from investigation through permanent resolution. You will also translate recurring support patterns into automation, self-service capabilities, and engineered solutions that reduce repetitive work and improve time to resolution.

About the Role

In this opportunity as a Senior Workplace Engineer – Microsoft 365, you will:

  • Provide Senior Support for M365, Copilot & AI: Act as the senior escalation point for Microsoft 365 across Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and the wider M365 administration surface. Own hands-on support, configuration, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management for Microsoft Copilot and Thomson Reuters' broader AI tooling for internal users. Diagnose and resolve identity, licensing, policy, and integration issues across the M365 and AI service layer.
  • Resolve Complex Escalations End to End: Independently resolve complex, cross-service escalations at the third-line level. Provide senior technical guidance to L1 and L2 support teams, conduct root-cause analysis for recurring incidents, and drive issues to permanent resolution rather than passing them to other teams. Maintain knowledge articles, runbooks, and support documentation to improve first-line and second-line effectiveness.
  • Drive Engineering & Automation: Build automation using PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, Power Platform, and equivalent tools to eliminate repetitive support work and maintain configuration consistency. Design and deliver AI-enabled support and self-service capabilities that deflect support volume and improve time to resolution. Convert recurring incident patterns into engineered, permanent fixes.
  • Partner Across Endpoint, Identity & Workplace Services: Operate effectively across the endpoint estate, including Intune-managed devices and modern management, where these services intersect with M365 and AI tooling. Partner with endpoint and identity teams to resolve cross-domain issues end to end.
  • Improve AI Productivity Tool Adoption & Reliability: Support the adoption, governance, and reliability of AI productivity tools. Translate technical capabilities into measurable employee outcomes while ensuring services are reliable and effectively supported across the internal workforce.
  • Communicate Technical Solutions Clearly: Explain technical resolutions to non-technical users, provide guidance to L1 and L2 teams, and apply sound judgment when determining whether an issue requires a tactical resolution or a permanent engineering solution.

About You

You're a fit for the role of Senior Workplace Engineer – Microsoft 365 if you have the following required qualifications:

  • 5+ years of IT support and engineering experience, including 5 years in End User Computing across a modern enterprise environment.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer science, systems engineering or related fields, or equivalent experience.
  • Minimum of 3 years of hands-on Microsoft 365 experience, including configuration, administration, troubleshooting, and third-line support across the core service set.
  • Demonstrable hands-on experience with Microsoft Copilot and/or comparable enterprise AI productivity tools.
  • Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert (MS-102) certification, or equivalent demonstrable Microsoft 365 expertise.
  • Automation and scripting experience using PowerShell and Microsoft Graph.
  • Working knowledge of endpoint management, including Intune and modern management, as well as enterprise identity through Entra ID.
  • Proven experience resolving complex, cross-service escalations independently and translating recurring problems into automated or engineered solutions.
  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills.
  • Customer-service orientation with a focus on the internal employee experience.
  • Ownership mindset and the ability to drive issues to closure without escalation upward.

Additional preferred qualifications include:

  • Microsoft Copilot or AI-related credentials.
  • Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator certification for Entra ID.
  • Microsoft Endpoint Administrator certification (MD-102) or equivalent Intune expertise.
  • Experience supporting AI-enabled self-service capabilities and automation within an enterprise workplace environment.
  • Experience working across M365, endpoint, and identity service domains.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 6–12 months, success in this role includes:

  • Complex Microsoft 365 and Copilot escalations resolved at the source and closed at the third-line support level.
  • A measurable reduction in repeat incidents through delivered automation and permanent engineering fixes.
  • Reliable AI productivity tooling with adoption across the internal workforce.

What’s in it For You?

  • Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
  • Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
  • Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
  • Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
  • Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.
  • Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.
  • Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

About Us

Thomson Reuters informs the way forward by bringing together the trusted content and technology that people and organizations need to make the right decisions. We serve professionals across legal, tax, accounting, compliance, government, and media. Our products combine highly specialized software and insights to empower professionals with the data, intelligence, and solutions needed to make informed decisions, and to help institutions in their pursuit of justice, truth, and transparency. Reuters, part of Thomson Reuters, is a world leading provider of trusted journalism and news.

We are powered by the talents of 26,000 employees across more than 70 countries, where everyone has a chance to contribute and grow professionally in flexible work environments. At a time when objectivity, accuracy, fairness, and transparency are under attack, we consider it our duty to pursue them. Sound exciting? Join us and help shape the industries that move society forward.

As a global business, we rely on the unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences of all employees to deliver on our business goals. To ensure we can do that, we seek talented, qualified employees in all our operations around the world regardless of race, color, sex/gender, including pregnancy, gender identity and expression, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, age, marital status, citizen status, veteran status, or any other protected classification under applicable law. title: Principal
description:
Overview

Voices is a public charter school network with a mission to prepare all learners for the challenges of higher education through the context of an academically rigorous dual-immersion program. Every learner, regardless of home language, graduates bilingual and biliterate through our full-inclusion English and Spanish dual-language model.

Though 90% of Hispanic young adults say that a college degree is important for success in life, fewer than 20% aged 25 or older hold a bachelor’s degree. In contrast, only about 35% of the general American public considers college highly important, and a similar 35% hold a bachelor’s degree (2023, 2024 Pew Research) Voices College-Bound Language Academies exists to change that.

Our educational philosophy is grounded in a sociocultural approach to learning that emphasizes collaboration, language development, and culturally sustaining practices. We believe students learn best in rigorous, language-rich environments that are developmentally responsive—prioritizing play-based pedagogy in early childhood and intentional direct and interdisciplinary instruction in the upper grades. Instruction is standards-based and designed to develop bilingualism, biliteracy, and critical thinking through reflective, data-informed practice.

If our mission, model, and approach to teaching and learning resonate with you, we invite you to apply.

Role Summary

Voices Academies’ Principal will be an inspiring and motivating instructional leader who can work independently. Reporting to the Principal Manager, the Principal forms part of the school’s leadership team. The principal oversees Teachers, Associate Teachers, and school support staff. The ideal candidate will have an unwavering commitment to ensure that students receive quality instruction, make accelerated educational progress, and reach or exceed their academic goals. The Principal is responsible for Voice’s academic, operational, fiscal, and organizational management and success. This includes supervising instruction and conducting the evaluation program for all staff. This interaction will include providing guidance and support in the classroom as appropriate. The Principal interacts extensively with teachers, staff, students, parents, the CEO, Board members, and the community through site-based management. Additionally, the Principal will be expected to meet specific performance objectives which may include such areas as academic, and financial goals in accordance with the Charter.

Key Responsibilities

Principal:

  • Submits to the CEO recommendations relative to all matters requiring Board action or attention, together with the materials needed for informed decisions
  • Reports on school operations to COO
  • Interview, train, supervise, and evaluate staff
  • Develop and implement a school-wide and individual staff development plan and provides ongoing support and coaching to teachers to help them meet their individual professional development plan goals
  • Coordinates the work of all school educators and volunteer staff
  • Advise the CEO or/and COO regarding the leave, classification, resignation, promotion, suspension or dismissal of school employees
  • Assigns personnel within the school in accordance with Board policy
  • Maintains appropriate channels of communication within the school and ensures that staff is informed about relevant federal, state, and county laws, policies, regulations, and procedures, and matters related to the improvement and welfare of the students
  • Plans, leads, and conducts staff professional development and staff meetings
  • Manage and/or oversee all daily school operations, including student admissions and discipline, facilities, food service, front office, school scheduling, etc.

Students and the educational program:

  • Serve as the school’s instructional leader, including ensuring that the school's mission and instructional program are being effectively implemented in each classroom
  • Monitor the school’s instructional and operational accountability, including collecting, analyzing, and reporting school and student performance data
  • Use this data (instructional and operational accountability) to develop school priorities and to drive decision-making
  • Enforces compulsory attendance laws
  • Continuously observes the instructional program and provides the CEO with regular evaluations of school programs and student progress
  • Studies the curriculum and makes decisions regarding the course of study, major changes and time schedules, and sound programs
  • Under appropriate circumstances, recommends to the Board a student’s suspension or expulsion
  • Participates in student study teams and IEP meetings

Non-instructional Operations:

  • Maintains and updates adequate census and scholastic records, business and property records, and personal records as applicable
  • Annually prepares and submits to the Financial Department the school’s budget for the upcoming year, revises this budget or takes other related action as the Board /CEO designates
  • Approves all expenditures in accordance with Board policy and within Board-approved appropriate limits
  • Makes recommendations to the CEO regarding the maintenance, safety, improvement and/or expansion of school facilities, sites, and equipment

Community:

  • Represents and advocates for the Board in relationships with city, county and state governments, private agencies, and the school community
  • Sees that the community is informed about school matters through appropriate informational materials
  • Serves on local committees such as ELAC, VPAC, Schools Leadership, etc.
  • Participates in appropriate community organizations and functions to obtain support for the attainment of school goals
  • Hears complaints against the school and solves controversies between employees or between employees and students or parents/guardians
  • Develops and maintains cooperative, collaborative working relationships with and among various stakeholders, including staff, students, families, Board members, District personnel, and the broader community
  • Facilitates and builds community among people from diverse backgrounds and perspective
  • Other duties as assigned

Voices Academies Principal candidates will have the following

Required Qualifications:

  • BA/BS Degree in Education or related field
  • CA Teaching Credential. Out-of-state equivalent credentials are accepted if they are transferable to a California credential. Mandatory enrollment in the next available Induction cycle upon hiring.
  • Valid California Administrative Services Credential required or currently enrolled in an admin credential program.
  • A minimum of five years of successful teaching experience at the appropriate TK–8 grade level.
  • Demonstrated classroom-level achievement results
  • Skilled in fiscal management
  • Demonstrated passion for the mission, vision, and values of Voices Academies with a deep commitment to improving the lives of students from low-income communities
  • Minimum three years working with similar student and community demographic
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills in English and Spanish
  • Outstanding written, speaking, and organizational skills with experience interacting with a broad range of stakeholders
  • Commitment to the accelerated educational progress of children
  • Experience or commitment to public education, social justice, efficacy, and equity
  • Ability to work well within a team environment; working efficiently, and exercising excellent judgment in making decisions
  • Works well in a high-pressure environment

Personal and Professional – Finally, the ideal candidate will hold the following personal and professional competencies:

  • Leadership – Couple strong management with excellent interpersonal skills in leading an organization in one’s functional domain
  • Relationship – Develop relational trust across constituencies, by maintaining a positive attitude with students, parents and staff, while also maintaining confidentiality
  • Organization – Be intensely execution-oriented and frighteningly organized, allowing one to work in a fast paced, but sometimes unpredictable, environment
  • Perspective – Combine maturity, humility, a strong work ethic, a sense of humor, and a roll-up-my sleeves attitude to celebrate successes as well as navigate times of ambiguity and high levels of stress
  • Professionalism – See oneself as an ambassador of the school, presenting oneself both positively and professionally at all times and with all constituents

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Masters Degree in Education
  • Bilingual Authorization (BCLAD/CLAD) preferred.
  • Knowledge of and experience working with low-income communities preferred
  • Proven track record of success managing school employees to achieve ambitious goals
  • Can work independently, have flexibility, and a demonstrated success in Administration, Organizational Management
  • Successful completion of results-oriented leadership training program (ex. Innovate Fellowship, NLNS)
  • Understanding of dual immersion instructional practices and school design and the unique characteristics of public charter schools is a plus
  • High proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Google Apps

Working Conditions:

  • Regular requirement to stand, sit, walk, talk, hear, see, read, speak, reach, stretch with hands and arms, stoop, kneel and crouch
  • Lift and carry objects weighing up to 50 lbs.
  • Occasional evening and or weekend work
  • Occasional travel
  • Willingness to be trained as needed

Prior to Employment: Once an offer has been extended, a candidate must meet the following criteria to receive a final agreement:

  • First Aid/CPR/AED Certification
  • Clear Criminal Background Check
  • Valid TB Clearance

Key Compensation:

  • Annual Salary Range: $120,000 - $145,000
  • Medical benefits
  • Exceptional growth opportunities
  • Retirement plan

Employment:

  • Reports directly to assigned supervisor
  • Full-time, exempt position
  • Position follows a 12 month calendar
  • At-Will Agreement


If you have any questions about this position, please contact our hiring team by email at jobs@voicescharterschool.com.


Voices College-Bound Language Academies will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities to enable them to perform the essential functions of the position, in accordance with applicable federal and California law.

title: Quality Operations System Auditor Intern, Spring 2027
location: Lake Buena Vista, Florida, United States of America
description:
About the Role & Program

"We make Magic!" That’s our motto at Walt Disney Parks and Resorts. And it permeates everything we do. At Disney, we help encourage that magic by enabling our teams to push the limits of entertainment and build the never-before-seen!

The approximate dates of this internship are January 2027 – June 2027.

What You Will Do

Our Quality Operations team is responsible for physically auditing the performance of cast and leadership within the Walt Disney World Resorts supporting Disney Springs, Disney Sports, Disney Water Parks, Disney Transportation, Disney Premium Services, Disney Parks & Resorts. Policies, procedures, processes, standards and interactions are evaluated providing valuable data to uphold the Disney standards.

In addition to the Resorts in Central Florida this dynamic team travels to Disney’s Vero Beach Resort and Disney’s Hilton Head Resort to provide senior leaders audits to assess service levels. As part of this team you will:

  • Participate and conduct audits across the Walt Disney World Resorts.
  • Develop, and coordinate the company’s compliance with internal requirements & processes.
  • Present findings to senior leaders in a capstone project.

Required Qualifications & Skills

  • Ability to partner with other teams and act with integrity.
  • Strong oral/written communication skills.
  • Excellent organizational and partnership skills.
  • Your prior experience as a foundation for learning the resort business.
  • Quick problem solver that crafts situations.
  • Deadline driven, time management and structure is their responsibility.
  • Ability to build positive relationships with operation leaders and cast.
  • Strong communication and comfortable communicating with executives.
  • Open and flexible to ad hoc projects.
  • Tech savvy with an ability to learn new applications.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Data Entry or Audit experience
  • Comfortable working with Microsoft Office (PowerApps, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.)
  • Disney alumni preferred

Education

  • Currently enrolled as a Junior, or higher, or have graduated within the past 6 months from an accredited college/university, earning a degree majoring in Hospitality, Marketing, Business or related area.

Job Description: Core Services & Server Operations Task Lead

GDIT is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Core Services Task Lead to oversee the management and delivery of enterprise-wide IT services for our client at USCENTCOM on the CITS contract. The Lead will be responsible for ensuring outstanding service quality, efficiency, and alignment with organizational objectives across multiple critical domains, including Server Infrastructure, Endpoint Security (ESS), E-discovery, Microsoft Configuration Manager (MCM), Monitoring (Observability), Storage, and VMware teams. This role will involve leading and coordinating various IT teams, establishing service management best practices, and driving continuous improvement initiatives to meet the strategic objectives of USCENTCOM.

HOW A CORE SERVICES TASK LEAD MANAGER WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:

Duties and Responsibilities:

We are seeking an experienced Lead with a strong background in coordinating IT service management tasks. The Lead will be responsible for:

• Overseeing the delivery of enterprise-wide IT core services, ensuring project goals, timelines, and objectives are met without disruption to ongoing command operations.
• Providing technical oversight and direction for the Server Infrastructure team, managing the daily administration, health, and security posture of enterprise Windows and Linux server environments.
• Providing direct oversight for the MCM team to ensure effective software deployment and patch management across the enterprise.
• Leading the Endpoint Security Solutions (ESS) team to protect systems from unauthorized access and vulnerabilities.
• Guiding the Observability (Monitoring Tools) team to ensure high availability and reliability through proactive system performance monitoring.
• Directing the Storage team in managing enterprise storage arrays, capacity planning, and maintaining critical backup infrastructure to prevent data loss.
• Overseeing the VMware team in deploying, optimizing, and securing the hypervisor cluster architecture supporting enterprise workloads.
• Managing the E-discovery support workflow, ensuring forensic data isolation and collection protocols adhere strictly to compliance and search mandates.
• Managing service delivery processes, such as incident, problem, change, and configuration management, adhering to ITIL best practices.
• Leading and mentoring IT teams responsible for service delivery, fostering a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer satisfaction.
• Developing and implementing service improvement plans to enhance service quality, efficiency, and effectiveness.
• Coordinating and managing service transitions, including service design, build, testing, and deployment, ensuring minimal disruption and risk to the business.
• Building and maintaining strong relationships with key stakeholders, understanding their needs, and driving service delivery improvements.
• Maintaining and Reporting on Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
• Establishing Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) w/ the customer to ensure service quality and efficiency.
• Ensuring compliance with security policies, regulations, DoD guidelines, and best practices related to enterprise services.

Additional Responsibilities:

• Leading Tiger Teams during high-pressure events to quickly resolve critical infrastructure outages, and providing training to junior Systems Administrators.
• Developing and updating comprehensive documentation related to enterprise services, processes, and procedures that aligns with a Cross Function Team (CFT) approach.
• Evaluating and recommending new technologies, tools, and methodologies to improve service delivery, efficiency, and scalability.
• Identifying potential risks affecting core services and developing mitigation strategies to minimize impact on project delivery.
• Supporting projects to enhance the security, efficiency, or capability of the enterprise services environment.
• Collaborating with vendors and third-party providers for troubleshooting and issue resolution.
• Monitoring and reporting on service performance, identifying trends, and preparing regular status reports for senior management proposing corrective actions to address potential issues.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO SUCCEED

Education and/or Certifications: Required:

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, or a related field OR equivalent experience.
• Applicable DoD 8140 or DoD 8570 Certification (to meet baseline security requirements).

Desired:

• Master’s degree in business administration, Information Systems, or a related field.
• Experience working in a cloud environment (e.g., AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud).
• ITIL 4 Managing Professional (MP), ITIL v3 Expert certification, or ITIL 4 Foundation.
• Advanced Certifications: Microsoft Windows Hybrid Administrator, Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator, VMware Certified Professional (VCP), Red Hat Certified Engineer (RHCE), or Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA).

Required Skills:

• At least 5+ years of experience as a Systems Administrator or in a similar leadership role managing enterprise environments.
• Demonstrated expertise in IT service management, including experience in leading IT teams and managing enterprise-wide services.
• Strong experience with Linux/Unix and Windows systems administration, and virtualization technologies (VMware, Hyper-V).
• Strong understanding of IT service management best practices, processes, and tools (e.g., ITIL, Remedy, and/or ServiceNow).
• Experience in service delivery performance management, including SLA development, monitoring, and reporting.
• Ability to build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, understanding their needs, and driving service delivery improvements.
• Experience in managing service transitions, including service design, build, testing, and deployment.

Desired Skills:
