title: Senior Regulator – Primary Market and AIM Regulation
description:
Senior Regulator – Primary Market and AIM Regulation – Investigations and Enforcement

Role Profile

Primary Market and AIM Regulation (“PMAR”) is responsible for first line primary regulatory oversight of all of LSE plc’s markets operated in its capacity as a Recognised Investment Exchange. Playing a critical role in maintaining confidence in and the integrity of those markets, PMAR’s responsibilities include: providing advice to issuers, advisers and market participants concerning rules interpretation and application; dealing with regulatory queries; real time and post event issue resolution; development of Rulebooks and associated policy and guidance and investigating suspected non-compliance and complaints.

Comprising experienced lawyers, accountants and regulators, the team manages a wide portfolio covering all key aspects of Primary market operation of AIM, the International Securities Market (“ISM”) and the Private Securities Market (“PSM”); investigative and disciplinary activity and regulatory input into LSE plc projects, products and market development.

This Senior Regulator role primarily focusses on investigative and enforcement (“I&E”) activity relating to potential non-compliance with the obligations and responsibilities contained in the AIM Rules for Companies and for Nominated Advisers (the “AIM Rules”), the ISM and PSM Rules and the Rules of the London Stock Exchange. Working as part of a specialist, multi-skilled team, the role involves proactive day-to-day individual responsibility and accountability for a broad caseload of a varying degrees of complexity, working in close partnership with more senior-level colleagues to deliver the I&E portfolio. The role may also involve supporting the real-time work of PMAR’s Operations and Guidance team, contributing to thematic and assurance work and to wider Market Regulation projects and initiatives as required.

Reporting to the Director of I&E and the Head of PMAR, the role provides a unique opportunity to develop insight, knowledge and expertise of all of LSE plc’s operated markets and involvement in all aspects of the teams work.

The successful candidate should be able to demonstrate a track record of an interest and ability to learn and develop technical knowledge and expertise (ideally in a legal or accounting context), apply sound judgment and a desire to gain experience of working in a fast-paced, collaborative, environment.

Key Responsibilities

I&E, complaints and enquiries:

· Pro-actively formulates and pursues enquiries into potential non-compliance with our Rulebooks including scoping, development of case strategies and information gathering.

· Manages communications with issuers, advisers and market participants and their representatives.

· Undertakes analysis, assessment and robust forensic scrutiny of information and evidence gathered through formal information requests, interviews and intelligence.

· Delivery of audience-tailored verbal and written presentation of findings, evidential analysis and recommendations of proposed actions.

· Preparation of fully evidenced written outcomes - from rules education and findings of non-compliance through to fomal disciplinary action ranging from warning notices and statements of case to pursue more material sanctions.

· Lead or assist with the preparation and case presentation before case governance and disciplinary committees.

· Contributes to the development of protocols amd operating procedures, policy and guidance and supports adherence to operational controls and governance.

· Supports and nutures relationships with other business areas and functions, external legal counsel and other regulators or law enforcement.

· Assesses and responds to information and concerns raised by market participants and investors.

Eligibility and ongoing assurance work:

Contribute to compliance and thematic reviews of nominated advisers.

Projects and research:

Involvement in project work, such as development of I&E frameworks for new products or markets. Undertaking research on new issues or trends as they arise and thematic work in relation to LSE plc’s Primary Markets portfolio

Key Behaviours

Communication - Oral and written communications are tailored to their audience’s needs;

Maximising opportunities - Open to and willingly adopts new processes / approaches / ways of working. Seeks information/inputs from colleagues/clients;

Excellence - Willingly puts in the effort to ensure activities completed on time and to the quality required. Pro-active and demonstrates initiative and personal accountability for all assigned responsibilities.;

Partnership, collaboration and change - Demonstrate confidence dealing with internal and external relationships; implement project management methodologies and keep colleagues and management updated on work progress.

Analysis & Problem Solving - Analyses issues to identify the most appropriate solutions. Utilises all available resources and toolsets to investigate and resolve problems;

Delivery - Prioritises and manages a diverse and varied workload. Takes on routine tasks as necessary. Carries out work without prompting and close supervision.

Flexibility – open to expanding knowledge of all market offerings, becoming a cross portfolio specialist.

Key Skills (Essential)

· Educated to degree level or equivalent. Ideally a qualified accountant or lawyer or with compliance or investigative experience gained in a financial institution or with another regulator. Part qualified candidates with demonstrable transferrable skills will be considered

· Good level of understanding of the UK financial services landscape and regulation and an interest in regulation.

· MS Office skill particularly in Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint and sharepoints, with a developing knowledge or familiarity of AI tools

Project Title
NAND Component Test Flow Optimization Using AI-Enabled Data Analytics and Automation

Project Description
The intern will participate in a structured Product Development Engineering project focused on optimizing NAND component test flows using manufacturing data analytics, automation, and Artificial Intelligence.

Under appropriate guidance, the intern will develop analytical tools, models, and visualizations to study manufacturing data, identify product recovery opportunities, and improve test-flow efficiency. The project will provide practical exposure to data engineering, statistical analysis, machine learning, prompt engineering, and the responsible application of enterprise AI tools.

Objective of the Project
The project aims to:

  • Improve the analysis of manufacturing and test-flow data.

  • Identify data-driven opportunities to enhance product recovery.

  • Develop automation solutions that improve engineering analytical efficiency.

  • Apply statistical, machine learning, and AI-Enabled methodologies to generate actionable insights.

  • Evaluate emerging Artificial Intelligence technologies for relevant engineering and manufacturing use cases.


Project Scope
The intern will be given the opportunity to:

  • Retrieve, prepare, analyze, and visualize manufacturing data to evaluate NAND component test-flow efficiency and product recovery opportunities.

  • Work with SpecTek engineers to understand test-flow challenges and apply structured, data-driven problem-solving methodologies.

  • Develop scripts, analytical models, reports, and automation solutions using relevant programming languages, statistical tools, and data platforms.

  • Apply statistical analysis, machine learning, enterprise AI tools, and prompt-engineering techniques to accelerate data exploration, knowledge retrieval, documentation, and insight generation.

  • Evaluate AI-Enabled solutions for engineering use cases, validate AI-generated outputs, and follow applicable data security, governance, and responsible AI requirements.

Learning Opportunities
The intern will have the opportunity to:

  • Gain practical exposure to NAND component testing, product recovery, and manufacturing data analysis.

  • Develop proficiency in programming, data preparation, statistical analysis, machine learning, automation, and visualization.

  • Learn how AI-Enabled tools and prompt-engineering techniques can be applied responsibly within engineering workflows.

  • Build experience in validating analytical and AI-generated outputs, documenting assumptions, and communicating limitations.

  • Strengthen critical thinking, technical documentation, stakeholder communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Deliverables
The intern is expected to deliver:

  • A structured analysis of NAND component manufacturing and test-flow data.

  • Scripts, analytical models, or automation tools for data preparation, analysis, and reporting.

  • Statistical or machine learning analyses identifying potential product recovery and test-flow improvement opportunities.

  • Visualizations and documented recommendations for engineering evaluation.

  • A final technical report and presentation covering the methodology, findings, validation results, limitations, and proposed next steps

Impact of the Project

The project is intended to:

  • Improve visibility into NAND component test-flow performance and product recovery opportunities.

  • Increase the efficiency and consistency of engineering data analysis.

  • Enable data-driven evaluation of potential test-flow improvements.

  • Strengthen the responsible use of automation and AI-Enabled analytics in engineering workflows.

  • Establish reusable analytical methods and tools for future engineering projects.

Skillsets Required
The ideal candidate should possess:

  • Programming knowledge in Python, C++,SQL, or equivalent analytical languages.

  • Familiarity with data analysis libraries and platforms such as Pandas, Perl, Hadoop, JMP, or equivalent tools.

  • Coursework or project experience in Artificial Intelligence, machine learning, data engineering, statistical analysis, or related areas.

  • Familiarity with AI-Enabled tools, coding assistants, prompt engineering, or data analytics platforms, including the validation of AI-generated outputs.

  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, problem-solving, collaboration, communication, and technical documentation skills.

Course of Interest
The ideal candidate should be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field.

Duration of Period
The ideal candidate should be able to commit to a full time internship period of 5 months from Jan to May 2027.

title: Senior Full-Stack / AI Platform Engineer
description:
Intuitive is building a new AI-powered platform to support how our teams work day to day — combining a
modern web application, cloud-native backend services, and generative AI to make information easier to
find, questions easier to answer, and repetitive work easier to automate.
We're looking for a senior full-stack engineer to help build this platform from the ground up, working across
the entire stack and partnering closely with the business teams who will use it every day. This is a hands-on
role for someone who wants to help shape a new product from its earliest stages — from architecture
decisions through to what the end user actually sees and uses.
What You'll Do
• Design, build, and maintain both the frontend and backend of a new internal platform, from early
prototypes through production
• Build and maintain integrations between the platform and its underlying cloud and AI infrastructure
• Partner directly with the business teams who will use the platform, translating their day-to-day workflows
into working software
• Implement secure authentication, access control, and data governance appropriate for sensitive
business data
• Help define and improve engineering practices — testing, CI/CD, deployment, and observability — as
the platform matures
• Iterate quickly based on real usage and feedback, balancing speed with reliability

What We're Looking For
• 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with real production ownership across both
frontend and backend systems
• Strong Python skills, with hands-on experience in FastAPI or a comparable async Python web
framework
• Strong React + TypeScript experience

• Experience integrating LLM/AI APIs into production applications — agentic or tool-calling patterns are a
strong plus
• Experience with a major cloud provider (Azure preferred; AWS/GCP experience with a willingness to go
deep on Azure also considered)
• Experience with OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authentication flows
• Comfort working directly with non-technical business stakeholders to shape product requirements from
ambiguous starting points
• Experience with CI/CD pipelines and containerized deployments
Nice to Have
• Experience with agent frameworks or tool-calling protocols (e.g., MCP)
• Experience with background job processing and Redis (or similar)
• Experience building products in a regulated or data-sensitive industry (healthcare, financial services, or
similar)
• Experience with enterprise document platforms (Box, SharePoint, or similar)
What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days
• Core platform infrastructure — authentication, the application shell, and the underlying data model — is
up and running
• The platform is answering real questions and handling real tasks for an initial group of users, with clear
traceability back to source data
• You're running regular working sessions with business stakeholders and have shipped the platform's
first end-to-end automated workflow

Open your soul to the heart of Mexico. With a prime location on the Pacific coast, Four Seasons Resort Punta Mita celebrates the rich culture of Mexico one epic sunset at a time. title: Lead Market Data Platform Engineer
description:
About this role:

Wells Fargo is seeking a Lead Market Data Platform Engineer within the Market Data Technology group. This role is responsible for the design, engineering, and support of mission-critical market data infrastructure platforms that deliver real-time and normalized pricing data across the enterprise.

The engineer will play a key role in supporting and enhancing the London Stock Exchange Group - The Refinitiv Elektron Platform (LSEG TREP) as well as related market data distribution technologies. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in market data systems, strong UNIX/Linux engineering capabilities, and a solid understanding of low-latency data delivery, networking, and vendor integration across providers such as LSEG, Bloomberg, and other market data platforms.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead or participate in high-level technical concepts spanning market data technology platforms and business consumption models

  • Design, build, and enhance complex market data infrastructure, including LSEG TREP and related distribution systems

  • Develop specifications, architectures, and solutions for low-latency, high-availability market data delivery platforms

  • Contribute to the testing and validation of market data flows, including feed handlers, distribution layers, and downstream consumers

  • Drive improvements in resiliency, failover, and recovery capabilities of market data systems

  • Analyze and resolve issues related to real-time data delivery, including feed gaps, latency, stale data, and symbology mismatches

  • Design and implement automation using UNIX/Linux scripting to monitor, manage, and maintain infrastructure health

  • Collaborate with network engineering teams to ensure optimal multicast/unicast data distribution, bandwidth utilization, and low-latency performance

  • Review and analyze infrastructure security considerations, including access controls, secrets management, and key rotations

  • Design, code, test, debug, and document tools and utilities to support market data operations and engineering functions

  • Support complex system upgrades, including TREP components, feed handlers, and supporting middleware

  • Identify and resolve recurring operational issues by implementing long-term engineering solutions

  • Develop and execute strategic plans to modernize and optimize market data platforms

  • Direct daily risk and control processes, ensuring adherence to enterprise policies, procedures, and regulatory standards

  • Collaborate and consult with peers, application teams, vendors, and leadership to resolve issues and deliver scalable, reliable solutions

Required Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of Technology Infrastructure Engineering and Solutions experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education

  • 4+ years of market data platform experience, including LSEG TREP

  • 4+ years of market data concepts experience, including real-time pricing, feed handlers, symbology, entitlements, and data normalization

  • 4+ years of UNIX/Linux engineering experience, including shell scripting (ksh, bash) for automation and operational support

  • 2+ years of networking experience, including TCP/IP, multicast, and low-latency data transport concepts

  • 2+ years of experience with monitoring tools and observability practices for real-time systems such as Grafana, ITRS

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience working with additional market data vendors such as Bloomberg, ICE, or Tradeweb

  • Understanding of market data feed formats and protocols (e.g., RIC Symbology, Elektron, proprietary vendor feeds)

  • Programming experience in Java, Python, or similar languages for tool and platform development

  • Experience with cloud technologies and hybrid infrastructure models

  • Familiarity with automation frameworks and infrastructure-as-code practices

  • Knowledge of financial markets, asset classes, and trading workflows

  • Experience with performance tuning and capacity planning for low-latency systems

  • Relocation assistance is not available for this position

  • Ability to support production environments, including participation in on-call rotations if required

  • Work closely with global teams, vendors, and stakeholders to support market data services

  • Adhere to Wells Fargo’s risk, control, and compliance requirements

  • Maintain strong documentation and audit readiness for all infrastructure components

title: Senior Premier Banker South Lakeline
description:
Why Wells Fargo:

Are you looking for more? Find it here. At Wells Fargo, we're more than a financial services leader – we’re a global trailblazer committed to driving innovation, empowering communities, and helping our customers succeed. We believe that a meaningful career is much more than just a job – it’s about finding all of the elements to help you thrive, in one place. Living the Well Life means you’re supported in life, not just work. It means having robust benefits, competitive compensation, and programs designed to help you find work-life balance and well-being. You’ll be rewarded for investing in your community, celebrated for being your authentic self, and empowered to grow. And we’re recognized for it – Wells Fargo once again ranked in the top five on the 2026 LinkedIn Top Companies list of best workplaces “to grow your career” in the U.S. Join us!

About this role:

Wells Fargo is seeking a Senior Branch Premier Banker (SAFE) to play a pivotal role within our National Branch Network. This role grows, deepens, and manages relationships with affluent customers and those with more complex financial needs, serving as their primary point of contact for banking products and services through scheduled appointments, lobby engagement, and proactive outreach. This role is designed for growth oriented professionals who lead with advice to acquire and deepen relationships through meaningful discovery and translate customer goals into comprehensive financial strategies. You will own and actively grow a defined book of business, leveraging goals based planning, and prudent risk oversight to deliver integrated solutions across deposits, investments, credit, home lending, and business banking. In addition, you’ll help customers with everyday banking needs-opening accounts, handling service requests, and ensuring a seamless experience making it easier for them to manage their banking with confidence. Success in this role is driven by strong relationship acumen, proactive customer engagement, and seamless collaboration with internal partners across Wealth, Home Lending, and Business Banking to deliver a differentiated customer experience.

Wells Fargo rewards behaviors that consistently create long term customer value and support customers in making informed financial decisions. You’ll be supported with digital tools, industry leading training, ongoing coaching, and backed by one of the most recognized brands in banking. This role offers a clear platform for career growth for experienced professionals who excel at building trust, managing a portfolio, and delivering holistic, multi product solutions.

In this role you will:

  • Proactively acquire new affluent consumer and business customers while deepening existing relationships through strategic outreach, referrals, and pre-planned customer appointments
  • Lead discovery‑driven conversations to understand customer goals and deliver tailored banking and credit strategies that strengthen relationships, increase retention, and drive balanced growth across deposits, lending, and investments
  • Serve as the primary financial partner delivering comprehensive, multi‑product guidance and ongoing reviews across life stages and evolving financial needs
  • Partner with a team of professionals across Wealth, Home Lending, and Business Banking to deliver integrated solutions by coordinating warm introductions, setting clear expectations, and taking personal ownership to convert qualified opportunities into closed outcomes
  • Champion digital adoption by educating customers on self-service and mobile banking options to elevate satisfaction, engagement, and service efficiency
  • Serve as an active member of the branch team by advising colleagues on relationship development and the management of complex client needs
  • Demonstrate risk excellence through accurate documentation, sound judgment, timely issue escalation, and adherence to policies and regulations to support strong control outcomes
  • The Senior Branch Premier Banker LP (license pending) role is a temporary position until employee has successfully completed licensing requirements and SAFE registration. Upon successful completion, employees will transition to the Senior Branch Premier Banker (SAFE) role. Employees hired into the Senior Branch Premier Banker LP role who are not fully licensed will participate in the Branch Network Licensed Banker program.

Required Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of customer service experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education
  • 3+ years of experience building and maintaining effective relationships with customers and partners
  • 3+ years of experience recommending products and services

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience recommending financial products and translating customer goals into clear, actionable recommendations
  • Demonstrated ability to proactively source, acquire, and deepen relationships through proactive outreach and building strong internal partnership to support the customer experience
  • Proven experience managing a book-of-business, documentation of planning conversations, and consistent follow-through to drive retention and growth across deposits, lending, and investments
  • Experience coaching or supporting peers to strengthen team performance and customer impact
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly and confidently, listen with empathy, and build credibility and trust quickly with others
  • Financial services industry experience in one or a combination of the following: consumer, home lending, business banking, or investments
  • 3+ years of experience in a licensed financial services position
  • Successfully completed Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA)Series 6 and 63 exams (or FINRA recognized equivalents) sufficient to qualify for immediate FINRA registration
  • State Insurance license(s)

Job Expectations:

  • Ability to work a schedule that will include most Saturdays
  • This role requires FINRA Series 6 and Series 63 (or FINRA recognized equivalents), and State Insurance license(s) which must be active or completed within a designated timeframe. For any FINRA qualification exams earned after Sept. 30, 2018, the Securities Industry Essentials (SIE) exam is also required.
  • For the following states where hired, FINRA Series 65 (or equivalent) examination will also be required within a specified period: AK, AL, CT, DE, HI, IA, ID, IN, KS, MD, MI, MN, MS, MT, NC, ND, NE, NM, OR, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI, and WY. Wyoming allows referral-only licensed bankers to receive the IAR registration without completing the Series 65/66 exam requirement. Requirements may change based on current state regulations.
  • Obtaining and maintaining required FINRA licenses is necessary for continued employment. This role also requires meeting enhanced financial fitness and criminal background standards. Wells Fargo will begin the FINRA review process once an offer is accepted.
  • SAFE registration is required at the time of employment and Wells Fargo will initiate the process after your start date. Loan Originators must meet LO/CFPB requirements and comply with Wells Fargo policies, including standards related to financial responsibility, character, fitness, and criminal background. A credit report may be reviewed (credit score not included) and additional ongoing screening may apply.
  • This position is not eligible for Visa sponsorship

title: Dragline Operator
description:
Reporting to the Dragline Supervisor, you will be responsible for the safe, professional and diligent approach and operation of our 8050 and 8750 Draglines. Applicants will possess appropriate mining operating experience including dragline, dozer, grader and cable reeler skills. You will display excellent interpersonal and communication skills along with an open mind and willingness to try new ways of operating.

To be successful in this role you will ensure compliance with all Anglo American safety and operating systems and a commitment to working together as part of a team to achieve business objectives. You will display excellent interpersonal and communication skills along with being a team player in safely achieving targets. You will be able to demonstrate your knowledge in dragline set up, operations and dig patterns to achieve machine optimization and improve performance.

  • You will possess at least 12 months competent dragline experience and be a proficient dozer operator.
  • You will be required to provide proof of your operating experience.
  • 7 on, 7 off, day and night rotating roster
  • Competitive Salary + 12% Superannuation
  • DIDO, Residential & Sal-sac FIFO options available
  • BIBO from Mackay and Rockhampton Area
  • Free Camp and Mess
  • Discounted Gym Membership
  • Free access to Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

What we offer
When you join Anglo American, you can expect to enjoy a competitive salary and benefits package and a range of flexible work arrangements that support the balance of work, family and individual circumstances. But more than this, you’ll find yourself in an environment where the opportunities for learning and growth are second to none. From technical training to leadership programs, we bring out the best in our people. There are plenty of opportunities to move onwards and upwards too.

Who we are
We aim to lead the industry by pursuing ever safer and more responsible ways of working, demonstrating integrity, and showing care and respect for people and the planet. That means we are constantly seeking new opportunities to mine and process our products sustainably, using less water, less energy and more precise extraction technologies. Anglo American is a leading global mining company focused on the responsible production of copper, premium iron ore and crop nutrients – future-enabling products that are essential for decarbonising the global economy, improving living standards, and food security. Our extraordinary teams work safely and collaboratively to unlock enduring value from precious natural resources for our shareholders, for the benefit of the communities and countries in which we operate, and for society as a whole. Anglo American is re-imagining mining to improve people’s lives.


Background checks
Successful candidates will be required to complete background screening which may include a criminal check and validation of qualifications.

Inclusion and Diversity
Anglo American is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promoting an inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are and provide equality of opportunity so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

How we are committed to your safety
Nothing is more important to us than ensuring you return home safely after a day’s work. To make that happen, we have the most rigorous safety standards in the industry. Not only that, we’re also continually investing in new technologies – from drones to data analytics – that are helping to make mining safer.

Employee referral
Do you know someone who would fit this role? Employee referrals will be accepted for this job. Refer to your local Referral Guidelines for policy conditions and amounts.

To apply for this role, please complete our online application form. You will have the opportunity to upload your CV and other relevant documentation as part of this process.

title: Speech Pathologist - Early Start Australia Graduate Program
description:
On the Early Start Australia Graduate program, you’ll feel all in from day one. In a close-knit allied health team, learning from each other and building lasting friendships along the way. With dedicated clinical supervision, mentoring and training, we’ll support you to grow with confidence – while making a positive impact in the lives of children and their families.

About the Graduate program

Our 12-month graduate program is designed to help you progress from student to thriving therapist. You can expect:

  • Structured induction with clinical skills training and a dedicated buddy.
  • Clinician shadowing before leading sessions independently.
  • Weekly supervision with an experienced clinician.
  • Supported ramp-up to managing your own caseload.
  • Learning and development built into your week.
  • Ongoing support from your multidisciplinary team and team leader.

What you’ll do at our Somerville clinic:

  • Deliver early intervention speech pathology services to children and families, supporting communication, participation, and independence.
  • Conduct comprehensive assessments (formal and informal) to identify speech, language, and developmental needs.
  • Develop and implement individualised, evidence-based therapy plans aligned with family goals and child needs.
  • Work collaboratively with families, caregivers, and multidisciplinary teams using a key worker/transdisciplinary approach.
  • Monitor, review, and adapt therapy programs based on client progress and feedback.
  • Provide education, resources, and ongoing support to empower families in decision-making and home-based practice.
  • Maintain accurate documentation, reports, and NDIS-related records within required timeframes.
  • Build strong relationships with stakeholders (e.g., schools, health professionals, support coordinators) to support client outcomes.

What you’ll get

Support

  • Dedicated buddy to help you settle in
  • 1:1 supervision with an experienced clinician
  • Discipline and peer-to-peer support sessions
  • Admin support so you can focus on learning and therapy

Grow with confidence

  • CPD allowance + paid professional development leave
  • Structured clinical and soft skills training
  • Clear path from graduate to independent clinician, and beyond
  • Local and global career opportunities through the APM Group

Flexibility and wellbeing

  • Up to 12 weeks annual leave
  • Flexible working options as you progress
  • Wellbeing support for you and your family

Reward and recognition

  • Competitive graduate salary + bonus program
  • Registration and professional membership contribution
  • Relocation reimbursement up to $5,000, where applicable

What you’ll bring

  • Relevant qualification in Speech Pathology
  • Membership / registration with relevant bodies (SPA)
  • Current Driver’s License and vehicle
  • Current Working with Children Check or Working with Vulnerable People Registration (state specific)
  • NDIS workers screening check & Police Check
  • Accredited first aid & CPR certificate
  • Strong communication and organisational skills
  • Exceptional observational and report writing skills

Who we are

We’re a passionate team of allied health professionals supporting children and young people to reach their full potential. Our multidisciplinary teams work closely with families to deliver fun, personalised, evidence-based support across communication, motor, cognitive and social development. We are a registered NDIS provider and our clinics offer therapy under different funding models. As part of the APM Group, you have the opportunity to grow your career in Human Services across multiple global brands and geographies. A diverse team of over 16,000 people across 11 countries with a shared purpose – to enable better lives for our employees and the communities we work in. Our work enables the people we serve to realise their ambitions and aspirations through sustainable employment, independence, better health and wellbeing and increased social participation.

Early Start Australia places a high priority on the principles of respect, equity and diversity. As an employer of choice, we strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders, people from culturally diverse backgrounds and people with disabilities.

title: CLO Deal Administrator
description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description

U.S. Bank Global Corporate Trust Services is one of the largest providers of corporate trust services in the world. Our clients look to us for trustee, agency, escrow, document custody and money market issuing services via our 48 domestic offices and three international offices.

The Collateralized Loan Obligation Group (CLO) is a division within Global Corporate Trust and Custody. CLOs are structured finance vehicles that issue both debt and equity liabilities, with the proceeds being used to buy a portfolio of collateral. Typical types of collateral include syndicated bank loans, corporate bonds, ABS, MBS, and Mezzanine debt. Investors can choose between a variety of risk return options.

The CLO Deal Administrator helps keep CLO portfolios running smoothly by handling the day‑to‑day operational work behind the scenes. This role supports daily and monthly reporting, tracks cash and par positions, settles trades, funds bank loans, and reconciles accounts to ensure all portfolio activity is accurate and complete. The administrator works with established processes, communicates regularly with internal teams and external clients via email and phone, and helps respond to routine client inquiries. It’s a fast‑paced, detail‑focused role that provides hands‑on exposure to CLO structures while building a strong foundation in financial operations through training and on‑the‑job learning.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary operational contact for assigned CLO clients

  • Perform frontline administration for CLO portfolios, ensuring accuracy and timeliness

  • Reconcile cash, positions, and portfolio activity across accounts

  • Apply and process wires (sending and receiving)

  • Settle bank loan and bond trades and manage trade lifecycle activity

  • Read and interpret deal notices and indenture-related documentation

  • Book cash inflows and outflows and invest excess cash as directed

  • Track asset attributes including accruals, ratings, and industry classifications

  • Produce and distribute daily, monthly, and quarterly client and investor reports

  • Communicate regularly with clients, portfolio managers, middle office teams, agents, and law firms

  • Manage high volumes of information and email in a fast‑paced environment

  • Identify, investigate, and resolve exceptions through analysis and problem‑solving

  • Support analysts with reporting and investor deliverables

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in finance or related field, or equivalent work experience

  • Typically less than two years of relevant work experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail

  • Basic understanding of indenture documentation and analytical skills

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and clients simultaneously

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills

  • Ability to interpret data and resolve discrepancies

  • High stress tolerance and resilience in a deadline‑driven environment

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel

  • Strong computer navigation skills across Microsoft Office applications

Location Expectations
The role offers a hybrid/flexible schedule, which means there's an in-office expectation of 3 or more days per week and the flexibility to work outside the office location for the other days. Office location is in Boston, MA.

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship, and does not support STEM OPT.

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate a disability during any portion of the application or hiring process, please refer to our disability accommodations for applicants.

Benefits:

Our approach to benefits and total rewards considers our team members’ whole selves and what may be needed to thrive in and outside work. That's why our benefits are designed to help you and your family boost your health, protect your financial security and give you peace of mind. Our benefits include the following:

  • Healthcare (medical, dental, vision)

  • Basic term and optional term life insurance

  • Short-term and long-term disability

  • Pregnancy disability and parental leave

  • 401(k) and employer-funded retirement plan

  • Paid vacation (from two to five weeks depending on salary grade and tenure)

  • Up to 11 paid holiday opportunities

  • Adoption assistance

  • Sick and Safe Leave accruals of one hour for every 30 worked, up to 80 hours per calendar year unless otherwise provided by law

Review our full benefits available by employment status here.

U.S. Bank is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or veteran status, and other factors protected under applicable law.

E-Verify

The E-Verify program is an Internet-based employment eligibility verification system operated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Learn more about the E-Verify program.

title: Miljö- och hållbarhetsspecialist till Fazer
description:
Fazer AB söker nu en engagerad och kompetent miljö- och hållbarhetsspecialist till vårt team i Tingsryd. I denna viktiga roll kommer du att spela en central del i våra strävanden att uppnå högsta standarder för miljöskydd och hållbarhet. Vi söker en person som har en stark passion för miljöfrågor och som vill bidra till utvecklingen av effektiva och hållbara processer inom livsmedelsindustrin.

Om rollen

Som miljö- och hållbarhetsspecialist kommer du att arbeta med att säkerställa att vi följer gällande miljölagstiftning och uppfyller våra hållbarhetsmål. Du kommer att ha ansvar för både kortsiktig och långsiktig planering och rapportering av miljöaktiviteter, samt driva utvecklingen av våra miljöprocesser. Rollen kräver ett nära samarbete med olika avdelningar och en aktiv närvaro i fabriksverksamheten för att kunna leda och implementera förändringar effektivt.

Kvalifikationer

För att lyckas i denna roll krävs följande kvalifikationer:

  • Kandidatexamen inom miljövetenskap eller motsvarande område (obligatoriskt).
  • Minst 3 års erfarenhet inom miljö- och hållbarhetsområdet, gärna inom livsmedelsindustrin eller liknande verksamhet (obligatoriskt).
  • Dokumenterad erfarenhet av ISO 14001 och efterlevnad av miljölagstiftning (obligatoriskt).
  • Mycket goda kunskaper i svenska och engelska, både i tal och skrift (obligatoriskt).
  • Erfarenhet från livsmedelsindustrin, mejeri, växtbaserade produkter eller kemisk industri (meriterande).

Arbetsuppgifter

Dina huvudsakliga arbetsuppgifter kommer att inkludera:

  • Ansvara för månatlig rapportering inom energi, miljö och hållbarhet.
  • Utveckla och implementera kortsiktiga och långsiktiga miljöaktiviteter.
  • Genomföra rotorsaksanalyser och miljöriskbedömningar av kemikalier och råvaror.
  • Följa upp verksamhetens påverkan på den externa miljön och rapportera driftstörningar till tillsynsmyndigheter vid behov.
  • Ansvara för uppföljning av periodiska besiktningar, tillsyn och revisioner.
  • Vara delaktig i implementeringen av ett energiledningssystem enligt ISO 50001.
  • Utveckla och sprida kunskap om företagets miljö och energiedningssystem till medarbetare.

Om Fazer

Fazer AB är en ledande aktör inom livsmedelssektorn i Norden och har ett starkt fokus på att erbjuda hälsosamma och hållbara produkter. Vår affärsenhet Fazer Plant Based Drinks är pionjär inom flytande växtbaserade livsmedel och har en lång historia av innovation. Vi strävar efter att skapa en positiv påverkan på både miljön och samhället genom våra verksamheter och produkter.

Vi erbjuder

Vi erbjuder en utmanande och utvecklande roll i en dynamisk arbetsmiljö där personlig säkerhet och professionell utveckling prioriteras. Som anställd hos oss får du möjlighet att leda betydelsefulla projekt och bidra till vår hållbarhetsstrategi. Vi erbjuder också konkurrenskraftiga förmåner och en arbetsplats som värdesätter dina insatser och engagemang.

Ansökan

Vi arbetar löpande med urvalsprocessen och uppmuntrar dig att skicka in din ansökan så snart som möjligt, då tjänsten kan bli tillsatt innan sista ansökningsdatum. Ansökan skickas via vår rekryteringspartner Flodin Rekrytering. Vi ser fram emot att ta emot din ansökan!

title: EHS Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
Job Summary

The EHS Engineer is responsible for supporting the implementation and continuous improvement of Environmental, Health, Safety, and Process Safety Management (PSM) programs across the Cairo Site. The role ensures compliance with local regulations, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 standards, IFF corporate requirements, and applicable process safety standards while promoting a strong safety culture, environmental sustainability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. The EHS Engineer partners with operations, maintenance, quality, and contractors to identify hazards, assess and reduce operational and process safety risks, support Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) and Management of Change (MOC) activities, improve environmental performance, and maintain a safe, compliant, and reliable workplace.

EHS Engineer

Cairo, Egypt | On-site | Full-time

At IFF, we make joy through science, creativity, and heart. As a global leader in food, beverage, health, biosciences, scent, and pharmaceutical solutions, we create ingredients that help make everyday products better for people around the world.

You will join a collaborative, supportive, knowledgeable, and highly engaged team that is passionate about safety, sustainability, and continuous improvement.

We are looking for an EHS Engineer to join our Cairo site. In this role, you will support the implementation and continuous improvement of Environmental, Health, Safety (EHS), and Process Safety Management (PSM) programs, ensuring compliance with local regulations, ISO standards, and IFF requirements while promoting a strong safety culture, environmental sustainability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Your Responsibilities

Safety Leadership & Culture

  • Promote a proactive safety culture through employee engagement, coaching, and awareness programs.
  • Support site EHS policies, procedures, and standards.
  • Lead safety campaigns, observations, and employee engagement initiatives.
  • Support Safety Committee activities and action plans.
  • Drive continuous improvement in site safety performance.

Risk Management & Compliance

  • Conduct workplace risk assessments, Job Safety Analyses (JSA), and task risk assessments.
  • Perform routine EHS inspections, audits, and workplace evaluations.
  • Monitor compliance with local regulations and IFF EHS requirements.
  • Track corrective and preventive actions and ensure timely closure.
  • Support implementation and maintenance of ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems.
  • Support Management of Change (MOC) activities and safety reviews for new projects.

Process Safety Management

  • Support implementation and continuous improvement of the site Process Safety Management (PSM) program, ensuring compliance with company standards.
  • Facilitate and participate in Process Hazard Analyses (PHA), including What-If, LOPA, Bow-Tie, HAC, and ATEX assessments, and drive timely closure of recommendations.
  • Support Management of Change (MOC), Pre-Startup Safety Reviews (PSSR), and process safety reviews for new projects, equipment, and process modifications.
  • Lead and support investigations of process safety incidents, near misses, and loss of containment events, identifying root causes.

Contractor Safety Management

  • Administer contractor safety programs and compliance requirements.
  • Conduct contractor inductions and site safety orientations.
  • Perform contractor audits and field safety inspections.
  • Monitor contractor performance and compliance with site EHS standards.
  • Support permit-to-work and contractor control processes.

Incident Investigation & Continuous Improvement

  • Lead and support incident investigations and root cause analysis activities.
  • Develop and track corrective and preventive actions.
  • Analyze trends and recommend improvement initiatives.
  • Share lessons learned and best practices across the site.

Emergency Preparedness & Fire Protection

  • Support maintenance and implementation of the Emergency Response Plan.
  • Coordinate emergency drills and exercises.
  • Support Emergency Response Team activities and training.
  • Conduct inspections of fire protection and emergency equipment.
  • Ensure emergency preparedness readiness and compliance.

Environmental & Sustainability Management

  • Support environmental compliance and sustainability initiatives.
  • Coordinate waste management, recycling, and waste reduction programs.
  • Support Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWL) initiatives and certification requirements.
  • Monitor energy, water, waste, and environmental performance metrics.
  • Support environmental permits, reporting, and regulatory compliance.
  • Assist in achieving site sustainability objectives and targets.

Training & Awareness

  • Deliver EHS training programs for employees and contractors.
  • Support new employee onboarding and EHS inductions.
  • Develop awareness campaigns and safety communications.
  • Maintain training records and competency matrices.

Performance Monitoring & Reporting

  • Track and report EHS performance indicators and metrics.
  • Prepare reports, dashboards, and presentations for site leadership.
  • Support internal and external audits.
  • Provide recommendations to improve EHS performance.

What You Will Need

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Chemical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
  • 3-5 years of experience in EHS roles within manufacturing or industrial environments.
  • Professional certifications such as NEBOSH, IOSH, or equivalent.
  • Experience implementing ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems.
  • Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and continuous improvement skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in manufacturing, chemical, food, flavors, pharmaceutical, or FMCG industries.
  • Experience with Process Safety Management (PSM).
  • Knowledge of What-If Analysis, LOPA, Bow-Tie, HAC, and ATEX assessments.

Why Join Us?

At IFF, we believe your uniqueness unleashes our potential. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where every colleague can thrive and contribute to meaningful innovations that improve everyday life.

Join a dynamic, passionate, caring, and committed organization where your expertise will help drive safety, sustainability, and operational excellence while making a positive impact on people and the planet.

We are a global leader in taste, scent, nutrition, health, and biosciences, offering exciting career development opportunities in an environment that values innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning.

Equal Opportunity Employer

IFF is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected characteristic

We are a global leader in taste, scent, and nutrition, offering our customers a broader range of natural solutions and accelerating our growth strategy. At IFF, we believe that your uniqueness unleashes our potential. We value the diverse mosaic of the ethnicity, national origin, race, age, sex, or veteran status. We strive for an inclusive workplace that allows each of our colleagues to bring their authentic self to work regardless of their religion, gender identity & expression, sexual orientation, or disability.

title: Senior Product Manager - Lending
description:
The Senior Product Manager - Build is responsible for shaping and launching Aussie Lending products and future lending capabilities, from early discovery and commercial feasibility through to operational readiness, go-live and handover into the Run team.

This role owns product discovery, strategy, roadmap and delivery across the Build portfolio. It defines the product construct, proposition, eligibility, features, pricing inputs, documentation and end-to-end customer and broker experience, while coordinating the systems, integrations, data, controls and operating model required to launch successfully.

Working across Lending, Strategic and Lending Partnerships, Technology, Data, Risk, Compliance and Operations, the role ensures each new product or capability is commercially sound, operationally viable and ready to run. Success is measured by disciplined delivery, accepted Build-to-Run handover and strong early-life product performance.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead product discovery, strategy, roadmap and end-to-end delivery for Aussie Lending products and future lending capabilities.
  • Lead the definition of the product construct, proposition, eligibility, features, pricing inputs, documentation and customer and broker experience.
  • Lead cross-functional delivery across systems, integrations, data, reporting, controls, training, testing, operational readiness, launch decisioning and go-live.
  • Lead the handover of each new capability into the Run team, including the handover plan, operating procedures, control evidence, service measures, training, ownership acceptance and post-launch performance loop.
  • Lead the Build roadmap for Aussie Lending products, including future enhancements, new products and new white-label opportunities.
  • Support the Head of Lending and Head of Strategic & Lending Partnerships with commercial negotiations for Aussie Lending products, including pricing options, partner economics and feasibility cases.
  • Lead the operational setup of new Aussie Lending products, ensuring the activities, roles, hand-offs, procedures, controls, reporting, governance, training, servicing and escalation pathways required to run them are in place.
  • Lead new lender and partner setup, including the operating model, delegated authorities, SLAs, KPIs, reporting, audit rights, incident pathways and change control.
  • Lead the setup of third-party agreements and integrations for services such as lenders mortgage insurance, valuations and identity platforms.
  • Lead end-to-end testing, operational readiness, launch decisioning, go-live and early-life performance management for Forward Flow.
  • Secure formal acceptance from the Run owners before any new capability is considered complete.
  • 5+ years’ experience in product management, including ownership of complex products or capabilities from discovery and strategy through delivery, launch and optimisation.
  • Demonstrated experience operating at Senior Product Manager level, with accountability for product strategy, roadmap prioritisation, delivery and measurable outcomes.
  • Strong experience in lending, mortgages or financial services; experience with lender products, white-label arrangements or forward-flow structures is highly desirable.
  • Proven ability to define product propositions, eligibility, features, pricing inputs, documentation and end-to-end customer or broker experiences.
  • Experience establishing operationally viable products, including operating models, procedures, controls, reporting, governance, training, servicing and escalation pathways.
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional delivery across Product, Technology, Data, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Finance, Operations and frontline stakeholders.
  • Experience leading third-party, lender or strategic partner setup, including commercial negotiations, agreements, integrations, delegated authorities, SLAs, KPIs and governance.
  • Strong commercial judgement, with the ability to develop feasibility cases, assess partner economics and support pricing and contract negotiations.
  • Strong technical and data fluency, with the ability to shape system integrations, data requirements, reporting, controls and implementation trade-offs.
  • Demonstrated experience leading end-to-end testing, operational readiness, launch decisioning, go-live and early-life performance management.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, stakeholder management and influencing skills, including the ability to align senior leaders and secure clear ownership acceptance.
  • Comfort working in ambiguity and fast-moving environments, with a disciplined approach to risk, prioritisation, handover and continuous product improvement.

title: CLO Deal Administrator
description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description

U.S. Bank Global Corporate Trust Services is one of the largest providers of corporate trust services in the world. Our clients look to us for trustee, agency, escrow, document custody and money market issuing services via our 48 domestic offices and three international offices.

The Collateralized Loan Obligation Group (CLO) is a division within Global Corporate Trust and Custody. CLOs are structured finance vehicles that issue both debt and equity liabilities, with the proceeds being used to buy a portfolio of collateral. Typical types of collateral include syndicated bank loans, corporate bonds, ABS, MBS, and Mezzanine debt. Investors can choose between a variety of risk return options.

The CLO Deal Administrator helps keep CLO portfolios running smoothly by handling the day‑to‑day operational work behind the scenes. This role supports daily and monthly reporting, tracks cash and par positions, settles trades, funds bank loans, and reconciles accounts to ensure all portfolio activity is accurate and complete. The administrator works with established processes, communicates regularly with internal teams and external clients via email and phone, and helps respond to routine client inquiries. It’s a fast‑paced, detail‑focused role that provides hands‑on exposure to CLO structures while building a strong foundation in financial operations through training and on‑the‑job learning.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary operational contact for assigned CLO clients

  • Perform frontline administration for CLO portfolios, ensuring accuracy and timeliness

  • Reconcile cash, positions, and portfolio activity across accounts

  • Apply and process wires (sending and receiving)

  • Settle bank loan and bond trades and manage trade lifecycle activity

  • Read and interpret deal notices and indenture-related documentation

  • Book cash inflows and outflows and invest excess cash as directed

  • Track asset attributes including accruals, ratings, and industry classifications

  • Produce and distribute daily, monthly, and quarterly client and investor reports

  • Communicate regularly with clients, portfolio managers, middle office teams, agents, and law firms

  • Manage high volumes of information and email in a fast‑paced environment

  • Identify, investigate, and resolve exceptions through analysis and problem‑solving

  • Support analysts with reporting and investor deliverables

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in finance or related field, or equivalent work experience

  • Typically less than two years of relevant work experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail

  • Basic understanding of indenture documentation and analytical skills

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and clients simultaneously

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills

  • Ability to interpret data and resolve discrepancies

  • High stress tolerance and resilience in a deadline‑driven environment

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel

  • Strong computer navigation skills across Microsoft Office applications

Location Expectations
The role offers a hybrid/flexible schedule, which means there's an in-office expectation of 3 or more days per week and the flexibility to work outside the office location for the other days. Office location is in Chicago, IL.

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship, and does not support STEM OPT.

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate a disability during any portion of the application or hiring process, please refer to our disability accommodations for applicants.

Benefits:

Our approach to benefits and total rewards considers our team members’ whole selves and what may be needed to thrive in and outside work. That's why our benefits are designed to help you and your family boost your health, protect your financial security and give you peace of mind. Our benefits include the following:

  • Healthcare (medical, dental, vision)

  • Basic term and optional term life insurance

  • Short-term and long-term disability

  • Pregnancy disability and parental leave

  • 401(k) and employer-funded retirement plan

  • Paid vacation (from two to five weeks depending on salary grade and tenure)

  • Up to 11 paid holiday opportunities

  • Adoption assistance

  • Sick and Safe Leave accruals of one hour for every 30 worked, up to 80 hours per calendar year unless otherwise provided by law

Review our full benefits available by employment status here.

  • Monitor, review, and adapt therapy programs based on client progress and feedback.
  • Provide education, resources, and ongoing support to empower families in decision-making and home-based practice.
  • Maintain accurate documentation, reports, and NDIS-related records within required timeframes.
  • Build strong relationships with stakeholders (e.g., schools, health professionals, support coordinators) to support client outcomes.

What you’ll get

Support

  • Dedicated buddy to help you settle in
  • 1:1 supervision with an experienced clinician
  • Discipline and peer-to-peer support sessions
  • Admin support so you can focus on learning and therapy

Grow with confidence

  • CPD allowance + paid professional development leave
  • Structured clinical and soft skills training
  • Clear path from graduate to independent clinician, and beyond
  • Local and global career opportunities through the APM Group

Flexibility and wellbeing

Reward and recognition

  • Accredited first aid & CPR certificate
  • Strong communication and organisational skills
  • Exceptional observational and report writing skills

Who we are

We’re a passionate team of allied health professionals supporting children and young people to reach their full potential. Our multidisciplinary teams work closely with families to deliver fun, personalised, evidence-based support across communication, motor, cognitive and social development. We are a registered NDIS provider and our clinics offer therapy under different funding models. As part of the APM Group, you have the opportunity to grow your career in Human Services across multiple global brands and geographies. A diverse team of over 16,000 people across 11 countries with a shared purpose – to enable better lives for our employees and the communities we work in. The roles are being recruited in response to growing student enrolments and increasing demand for Tertiary Foundation Certificate (TFC) English courses, with teaching at both our City and Te Tai Tonga (Manukau) campuses. One position is permanent and one is a three-year fixed term role.

As a Professional Teaching Fellow in TFC English, you’ll be at the heart of:

  • Teaching foundation-level English tailored to the diverse learning needs of TFC students and preparing them for undergraduate study in the humanities and across the University
  • Coordinating and teaching TFC English courses across in-person, asynchronous and blended delivery modes
  • Providing high-quality, research-informed learning and assessment, alongside pastoral support that is essential to enabling student success
  • Supporting students one-on-one, helping them build confidence and capability as they prepare for tertiary study
  • Contributing to course and curriculum development as TFC English continues to grow and expand across campuses and delivery modes
  • Contributing to a strong and collegial team culture across TFC, Humanities and English

The workload allocation for these positions is 80% teaching and 20% service.

There are two positions available:

  • One full-time (40 hours per week), permanent position
  • One full-time (40 hours per week), three-year fixed-term position

If you are only interested in one of the contract types, please indicate your preference in your covering letter. Otherwise, we will assume you are open to being considered for both positions.

For more information about this role, please refer to the Position Description.

He kōrero mōu | About you

The ideal candidate will hold a Masters or PhD in English or a related discipline and have experience teaching English in a high-school, college or university setting. We particularly value experience teaching in foundation-level or related programmes.

You will be confident coordinating courses and using a learning management system such as Canvas and enjoy working with learners at varying levels and from diverse backgrounds. You will communicate clearly, collaborate effectively and bring a positive, student-centred approach to your teaching. You are also keen to innovate, adapt and contribute to research-informed teaching and the continued development of TFC English.

Ngā āhuatanga kei a mātou | What we offer

As New Zealand’s largest, highest ranked and most comprehensive university, we are committed to supporting your career with:

  • Excellent teaching, research and campus facilities
  • 5 weeks annual leave
  • Up to 6.75% company superannuation scheme

In addition, we also offer career development programmes, discounted car parking, a generous parental leave allowance, childcare, and several discounts on internal and external services.

For more information, please visit Staff Benefits.

Me pēhea te tuku tono | How to apply

Applications must be submitted online by the closing date of Sunday 13 September 2026 (11.59pm).

Please include your cover letter and CV, including a teaching statement, teaching record, and (if applicable) summarised teaching evaluations.

Please reach out to Andrew Dawson (TFC Director) or Kim Phillips (HoS Humanities) for a confidential conversation. Please note that while we are happy to answer your questions, we do not accept applications by email.

title: Integration Architecture and Governance Senior Analyst
description:
Job Description:

Your Next Big Career Move Starts at DXC Technology

We’re Hiring: Integration Architecture and Governance Senior Analyst

Location: DXC Manila IPC McKinley Hill, Taguig City
Employment Type: Full Time

At DXC, we build strong connections, embrace innovation, and empower our people to grow. We’re looking for a Integration Architecture and Governance Senior Analyst who is motivated, skilled, and eager to contribute to meaningful projects.

Key Responsibilities

1. New Integration Request Assessment

  • Lead discovery and requirement-analysis sessions for integration requests received through ServiceNow.
  • Assess functional and non-functional requirements, dependencies, data flows, security, connectivity, error handling, observability and operational support needs.
  • Recommend appropriate integration platforms, patterns and solution options across API, messaging, streaming, MFT/B2B, SAP and iPaaS technologies.
  • Document assumptions, architecture decisions, risks, constraints and recommended next steps.
  • Coordinate clarifications and maintain accurate request status through completion.

2. Architecture and Governance Reviews

  • Conduct formal design architecture reviews, code reviews, test-results validation and risk assessments against approved standards and best practices.
  • Identify non-compliance, design weaknesses, operational risks and required remediation actions.
  • Provide clear review findings, approval recommendations and traceable evidence.
  • Escalate exceptions, high-risk decisions and cross-platform concerns to the Integration Architecture and Governance Architect.

3. Proofs of Concept and Project Assistance

  • Design and develop PoCs for new middleware patterns, technologies and complex integration scenarios.
  • Define PoC scope, success criteria, test approach and technical evaluation criteria with stakeholders.
  • Engage partner application, security, cloud operations and platform teams as required.
  • Document results, limitations, risks and production-readiness considerations; present recommendations for architecture approval.

4. Reusable Templates, Standards and Knowledge Assets

  • Convert approved PoCs and proven solutions into reusable templates, reference implementations and documented patterns.
  • Create and maintain integration standards, best practices, checklists, review guides and technical knowledge articles.
  • Facilitate alignment workshops and incorporate cross-platform updates for new technologies and patterns.
  • Provide knowledge transfer to implementation teams and analysts.

5. Technology Evaluation and Innovation

  • Evaluate new integration technologies, platform capabilities and architecture patterns.
  • Contribute to governance review automation, workflow automation and AI-assisted engineering initiatives.
  • Develop or enhance accelerators and utilities using Java, Python, PowerShell or relevant platform tooling.
  • Support API management, event-driven, streaming and cloud-native reference solutions.

6. Governance Metrics and Service Reporting

  • Maintain accurate ServiceNow and JIRA records for assessments, reviews, PoCs, risks, decisions and actions.
  • Contribute to Power BI dashboards, data validation, volume reporting, compliance measures and governance analytics.
  • Monitor assigned work against service targets and proactively address blockers or overdue dependencies.
  • Identify recurring issues and recommend process, standard or automation improvements.

7. Technical Leadership and Collaboration

  • Provide day-to-day technical guidance and quality review for Integration Architecture and Governance analysts.
  • Collaborate effectively with enterprise and integration architects, application owners, developers, platform operations, information security and cloud teams.
  • Communicate technical recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Participate in architecture forums, governance reviews and service-improvement planning.

Expected Deliverables

  • Integration assessment reports and solution recommendations
  • Architecture decision records, diagrams, assumptions, risks and dependency logs
  • Design, code and test governance review findings
  • PoC designs, working prototypes, test results and evaluation reports
  • Reusable templates, reference implementations and integration pattern documentation
  • Standards, best practices, checklists and knowledge articles
  • Technology and pattern evaluation reports
  • Automation utilities and governance process improvements
  • Accurate ServiceNow and JIRA records and contributions to Power BI reporting

Success Measures

  • Initial contact and assigned assessments completed in line with agreed Integration Architecture and Governance lead-time targets
  • Clear, complete and actionable recommendations with appropriate architecture approval
  • Consistent, evidence-based governance reviews and timely closure of findings
  • PoCs completed against agreed success criteria and converted into reusable assets where appropriate
  • High-quality documentation, traceability and stakeholder communication
  • Demonstrated contribution to standards improvement, automation, AI enablement and team capability growth

Qualifications

  • 5-7 years of experience in enterprise integration, middleware engineering, integration solution architecture or governance.
  • Deep hands-on expertise in at least one strategic integration platform and working knowledge of multiple others in the technology scope.
  • Proven experience designing enterprise-grade integrations across cloud, hybrid and on-premises environments.
  • Hands-on development, configuration and troubleshooting experience.
  • Experience conducting architecture reviews, design reviews, code reviews, test validation reviews and technical risk assessments.
  • Strong understanding of REST APIs, JSON, XML, XSD, OAuth, SFTP, messaging, event-driven architecture and integration security.
  • Knowledge of API-led architecture, messaging patterns, cloud-native integration patterns, DevSecOps, observability and resilience.
  • Ability to develop PoCs, reference architectures, reusable templates and technical standards.
  • Proficiency in Java and/or Python; PowerShell or JavaScript is beneficial.
  • Experience with ServiceNow and JIRA; exposure to Power BI or comparable reporting tools is beneficial.
  • Strong documentation, analytical, facilitation and stakeholder communication skills.
  • Ability to mentor less-experienced team members and work effectively in a global delivery model.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation and benefits

  • Professional growth opportunities

  • A collaborative and inclusive workplace

If this sounds like you, apply and take the next step in your DXC journey.
